item_inventory_ref.description: An inventory item is any merchandise or part that a business purchases, tracks as inventory, and then resells. In QuickBooks, information about an inventory item is grouped into three categories:Puchase Information includes PurchaseDesc, PurchaseCost, COGSAccountRef, and PrefVendorRef. Sales Information includes SalesDesc, SalesPrice, and SalesTaxCodeRef. Inventory Information includes AssetAccountRef, ReorderPoint, QuantityOnHand, TotalValue, and InventoryDate. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. An ItemInventoryRef aggregate refers to an inventory item. In a request, if an ItemInventoryRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_inventory_assembly_add.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.class_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.item_inventory_assembly_line.item_inventory_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_inventory_assembly_add.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.class_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.item_inventory_assembly_line.item_inventory_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_inventory_assembly_add.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.class_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.item_inventory_assembly_line.item_inventory_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_assembly_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

price_level_fixed_percentage.description:
When you create a price level, you must specify whether it is a fixed percentage or a per item price level. Once you create the price level, you can’t change this. QuickBooks Pro and greater versions support fixed percentages, but only QuickBooks Premier and Enterprise support the per item price level. Where is this discount applied if Price Levels are enabled in QuickBooks preferences? The discount is applied to the sales price of the item. If the price level is applied to a customer, it automatically adjusts the Rate and Amount columns for applicable line items in a QuickBooks Sales Order form, Invoice form, etc. for that customer. The QuickBooks user could still select a different price level. However, the customer price level simply establishes a default price. If no price level is applied to the customer, then the QuickBooks user can apply a price level by clicking the dropdown list of price levels that appears next to the Rate column. The default in this case is simply the sales price established for the item. Notice that this value supports both positive and negative values. For example, a value of 20 would increase the price by 20% and value of -10 would decrease the price by 10%.

Choose at most one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item_ret`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

price_level_per_item_ret.description: Choose at most one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item_ret`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (CustomPrice) or a fixed discount percentage (CustomPricePercent). Alternatively, instead of a flat custom price or discount, you could apply a price discount based on either the current custom price, the standard price of the item, or the cost of the item.

Choose exactly one of: `custom_price`, or `custom_price_percent`.

custom_price_percent.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (CustomPrice) or a fixed discount percentage (CustomPricePercent).

Choose exactly one of: `custom_price`, or `custom_price_percent`.

QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq. You should also save this transaction ID and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you are intending to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `inventory_site_add.parent_site_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `inventory_site_add.parent_site_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `inventory_site_add.parent_site_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

accountant_copy.description: Aggregate containing information about accountant copy. An Accountant’s Copy is a version of your company file your accountant can use to make changes while the original company file continues to be used for most normal operations. The key part of the accountant copy “protocol” is the dividing date which defines the fiscal period within which the accountant will be working. Dividing date is key because there are enforced restrictions against certain types of operations on data that fall within the fiscal period the accountant is working on.continue to work. The restrictions are listed below: Transactions: You can work only on transactions dated after the dividing date. Accounts: You can add a new account, but you can’t add a new subaccount to an existing account. Existing accounts: You can’t edit, merge, or make an existing account inactive. New accounts: You can edit an account or make any account inactive that you created while your accountant has the Accountant’s Copy. Lists (other than Chart of Accounts): You can edit, sort, and make list items inactive. You can’t delete or merge list items. Reconciling:You can reconcile your accounts while your accountant has an Accountant’s Copy. All reconciliations that include transactions in the current period (after the dividing date) are saved and won’t be undone. To prevent conflicts with your accountant’s changes, reconciliations that include transactions dated on or before the dividing date will be undone when you import your accountant’s changes. If your accountant has reconciled or undone a reconciliation for any period, any reconciliations you did will be undone when you import your accountant’s changes.

accountant_copy_exists.description: Indicates whether an accountant copy has been made for this company file, with a value of true meaning a copy has been made and a value of false meaning there is no accountant copy.

dividing_date.description: The dividing date indicates the fiscal period within which the accountant is working. This date is key because as long as the accountant copy exists, no transactions can be modified or created within that period. You can add new accounts, but you can’t add new subaccounts to existing accounts, and you can’t edit, merge, or make an existing account inactive. Finally, you can’t delete or merge list items.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `ar_refund_credit_card_add.ar_account_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.customer_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.payment_method_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.refund_from_account_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `ar_refund_credit_card_add.ar_account_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.customer_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.payment_method_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.refund_from_account_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `ar_refund_credit_card_add.ar_account_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.customer_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.payment_method_ref`, `ar_refund_credit_card_add.refund_from_account_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `vendor_add.additional_contact_ref`, `vendor_add.billing_rate_ref`, `vendor_add.class_ref`, `vendor_add.contacts.additional_contact_ref`, `vendor_add.currency_ref`, `vendor_add.prefill_account_ref`, `vendor_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `vendor_add.sales_tax_return_ref`, `vendor_add.tax_on_purchases_account_ref`, `vendor_add.tax_on_sales_account_ref`, `vendor_add.terms_ref`, `vendor_add.vendor_type_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `vendor_add.additional_contact_ref`, `vendor_add.billing_rate_ref`, `vendor_add.class_ref`, `vendor_add.contacts.additional_contact_ref`, `vendor_add.currency_ref`, `vendor_add.prefill_account_ref`, `vendor_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `vendor_add.sales_tax_return_ref`, `vendor_add.tax_on_purchases_account_ref`, `vendor_add.tax_on_sales_account_ref`, `vendor_add.terms_ref`, `vendor_add.vendor_type_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `vendor_add.additional_contact_ref`, `vendor_add.billing_rate_ref`, `vendor_add.class_ref`, `vendor_add.contacts.additional_contact_ref`, `vendor_add.currency_ref`, `vendor_add.prefill_account_ref`, `vendor_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `vendor_add.sales_tax_return_ref`, `vendor_add.tax_on_purchases_account_ref`, `vendor_add.tax_on_sales_account_ref`, `vendor_add.terms_ref`, `vendor_add.vendor_type_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `transfer_add.class_ref`, `transfer_add.transfer_from_account_ref`, `transfer_add.transfer_to_account_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `transfer_add.class_ref`, `transfer_add.transfer_from_account_ref`, `transfer_add.transfer_to_account_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `transfer_add.class_ref`, `transfer_add.transfer_from_account_ref`, `transfer_add.transfer_to_account_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `journal_entry_mod.currency_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.account_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.class_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.entity_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.item_sales_tax_ref`. * `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `journal_entry_mod.currency_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.account_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.class_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.entity_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.item_sales_tax_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `journal_entry_mod.currency_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.account_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.class_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.entity_ref`, `journal_entry_mod.journal_line_mod.item_sales_tax_ref`. * `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected. A QuickBooks admin has to remove the closing-date password (Accounting company preferences) before it can be changed.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.

* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.

* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `employee_mod.additional_contact_ref`, `employee_mod.billing_rate_ref`, `employee_mod.employee_payroll_info_mod.class_ref`, `employee_mod.employee_payroll_info_mod.earnings.payroll_item_wage_ref`, `employee_mod.supervisor_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `employee_mod.additional_contact_ref`, `employee_mod.billing_rate_ref`, `employee_mod.employee_payroll_info_mod.class_ref`, `employee_mod.employee_payroll_info_mod.earnings.payroll_item_wage_ref`, `employee_mod.supervisor_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `employee_mod.additional_contact_ref`, `employee_mod.billing_rate_ref`, `employee_mod.employee_payroll_info_mod.class_ref`, `employee_mod.employee_payroll_info_mod.earnings.payroll_item_wage_ref`, `employee_mod.supervisor_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `transfer_mod.class_ref`, `transfer_mod.transfer_from_account_ref`, `transfer_mod.transfer_to_account_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `transfer_mod.class_ref`, `transfer_mod.transfer_from_account_ref`, `transfer_mod.transfer_to_account_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected. A QuickBooks admin has to remove the closing-date password (Accounting company preferences) before it can be changed.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `to_do_mod.customer_ref`, `to_do_mod.employee_ref`, `to_do_mod.lead_ref`, `to_do_mod.vendor_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `to_do_mod.customer_ref`, `to_do_mod.employee_ref`, `to_do_mod.lead_ref`, `to_do_mod.vendor_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `to_do_mod.customer_ref`, `to_do_mod.employee_ref`, `to_do_mod.lead_ref`, `to_do_mod.vendor_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_inventory_mod.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.class_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. * `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_inventory_mod.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.class_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_inventory_mod.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.class_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_mod.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_sales_tax_add.class_ref`, `item_sales_tax_add.sales_tax_return_line_ref`, `item_sales_tax_add.tax_vendor_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_sales_tax_add.class_ref`, `item_sales_tax_add.sales_tax_return_line_ref`, `item_sales_tax_add.tax_vendor_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_sales_tax_add.class_ref`, `item_sales_tax_add.sales_tax_return_line_ref`, `item_sales_tax_add.tax_vendor_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage, such as which field it did not support.

code.description: QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

createItemOtherCharge_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

is_tax_included.description: For future use with international versions of QuickBooks.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

name.description: Name is the case-insensitive short name of a list object (without ancestors). It must be unique within its hierarchy scope. Hierarchical lists can reuse the same Name in different branches because FullName remains distinct.

parent_ref.description: A reference to the list object that is one level above this one. For example, an inventory item with the FullName of GermanCars:Mercedes-Benz:CL500I99AA might have a parent object with the FullName of GermanCars:Mercedes-Benz. In a request, if a ParentRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. txn_id.description: TxnID is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. TxnID values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

txn_number.description: An identifying number for this transaction.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_other_charge_add.class_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.parent_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.expense_account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.income_account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_or_purchase.account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_tax_code_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_other_charge_add.class_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.parent_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.expense_account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.income_account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_or_purchase.account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_tax_code_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_other_charge_add.class_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.parent_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.expense_account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.income_account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_and_purchase.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_or_purchase.account_ref`, `item_other_charge_add.sales_tax_code_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_service_mod.class_ref`, `item_service_mod.parent_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.expense_account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.income_account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_or_purchase_mod.account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_service_mod.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_service_mod.class_ref`, `item_service_mod.parent_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.expense_account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.income_account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_or_purchase_mod.account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_service_mod.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_service_mod.class_ref`, `item_service_mod.parent_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.expense_account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.income_account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_and_purchase_mod.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_or_purchase_mod.account_ref`, `item_service_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_service_mod.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

subtotal.description: The total of all the credit-memo lines, before taxes are applied. (By contrast, a subtotal item (an ItemSubtotal object) gives only the total of the amounts in the lines that appear above it.)

sales_tax_total.description: The total amount of sales tax charged.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

sales_rep_ref.description: A sales representative must be on the Employee, Vendor, or Other Names list within QuickBooks. owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

ship_method_ref.description: A shipping method, for example, standard mail or overnight delivery. A ShipMethodRef aggregate refers to an item on the ShipMethod list. In a request, if a ShipMethodRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.
