If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

deposit_to_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where these funds will be (or have been) deposited. In a ReceivePaymentAdd request, the default is Undeposited Funds if this isn’t included in the request. In a request, if a DepositToAccountRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

exchange_rate.description: ExchangeRate is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. You can supply a rate when adding transactions, but QuickBooks does not provide rates through the SDK. If your home currency is USD and internet access is available, rates can be downloaded in the QuickBooks UI via Lists > Currency > Activities > Download Latest Exchange Rates.

WorkflowUsage.description: Derived from the chart; nothing here is stored or hand-written.

child_outcomes.description: Per `workflow` state, every outcome the workflow it calls declares. A called workflow's ending arrives as an ordinary `success` (a declared failure as `error`) with `response.outcome` naming it, so a state that does not branch on it carries on as though nothing unusual happened. Each has `state`, `workflow`, `outcome`, `kind` (`success` or `failure`), `description`, `handled_at` (the state, or the state enclosing it, that branches on this outcome; `root on.success` or `root on.error` when the chart's root does; null when nothing does) and `per_item` (true when the state runs once per item, so each element's ending arrives in `response.outcomes` instead). Empty when the workflow calls none, or none that is installed.

decision_flow.description: How answering a question works, whatever the question: `asynchronous` (a run waits for an answer indefinitely); `delivery`, the `workflow_run.awaiting_input` webhook a question arrives in (`event`, where it is sent, `signature_header`, `answer_url` and the `payload` envelope); `answer`, the request that answers it (`method`, `path`, `auth`, a `body` template, `data_note` and `response`, plus, when the workflow asks anything, a `response_example` of answering its first question and an `error_example` of the 422 a wrong option gets); `poll`, reading the run instead of waiting for the webhook; `cancel`, stopping the run instead (its request, a `note` and its `errors`); `composed`, how a question asked by a workflow this one calls arrives (`applies` is true when this workflow has one); and `errors`, what the decisions endpoint can refuse an answer with (`status`, `code` and `meaning` each).

decisions.description: Every question the workflow may ask, including ones asked by workflows it calls (their ids are prefixed by the calling state). Each carries its `kind` (`decision` for a wait state's question, `conflict` for the prompt the engine asks when an update whose `on_conflict` is `ask` meets a stale edit sequence; those come after the wait states' and have id `conflict:<state>`), the message as authored (for a conflict, `when` says when it is asked), the options and their fields, a `webhook_example` of the payload it arrives in, one `answers` body per option, and `data`: per `prompt.data` key, where it comes from and an `example` of what it carries -- the record from the request that fills it when exactly one does, and a placeholder otherwise; for a conflict, a `description` of each key.

notifications.description: Every notify state the workflow can send the app data from, including those of workflows it calls (their `state` is prefixed by the calling state): `name` (what the app routes on), `description`, `state` (the webhook's `state`, its path from the run), `leaf_state` and `workflow` (where it is, in the workflow that sends it), `sent_by_child`, `per_item_of` (the calling state that runs once per item, when it is sent from inside one; null otherwise), `error_handled` (whether the workflow handles it not being delivered; otherwise the run fails), `data_example` (what `data` carries, from the chart: a record's identifying fields where it sends a request's response, placeholders for what only exists mid-run) and `webhook_example`, the whole `workflow_run.notification` it arrives in. A run of a workflow with any must be started with a `webhook_url`. Empty when it sends none.

outcomes.description: One entry per ending the run can reach: the successes, then the failures the workflow declares, then `failed`. Each has `outcome`, `kind` (`success` or `failure`), `description` and `from_states`, the states that lead there. A success carries `output_keys` and an `output_example`, and so does a declared failure with an output of its own: per key, its `values` when they are known (a key that is `${meta.outcome}` has the ending's own name), else `source`, the states whose responses feed it, with that operation's `shape` when there is one; `may_be_null` flags a key that may not be set. `completed` is listed only when something in the chart reaches it, or when the workflow declares no success of its own. A declared failure lists the `errors` it can carry; `failed` is always listed, with the messages this workflow can end with (`authored_errors`), the ones that carry a QuickBooks message or a called workflow's error through (`dynamic_errors`), and the engine's own (`engine_errors`).

per_item.description: One entry per `workflow` state that runs once per element of a list: `state` (its path), `workflow` (the key it calls), `each` (the list, as the chart writes it), `as` (the name each element is bound to; `item` unless the state names another), `on_item_error` (`stop` or `continue`), and `sentence`, the same said in one sentence. Empty when nothing in the workflow runs once per item.

request_errors.description: Per request state, the QuickBooks status codes its operation can raise and whether this workflow handles each one; `settle`, whether a request QuickBooks never answered is settled before the state raises anything; and `on_conflict`, for an update, what happens when the record changed after it was read (`ask`, `overwrite` or `fail`; null for anything that is not an update). A request state whose `operation` is a template (`${input.<name>.operation}`) is listed with `operation` null, `operation_template` the template and no codes, since the operation is decided when the run starts.

start.description: The request that starts a run: method, path, an example body, the input JSON Schema, and a note per declared input.

states.description: What each run state means, in lifecycle order.

webhooks.description: The webhooks a run of this workflow sends, each with `event` and `when`: `workflow_run.awaiting_input`, `workflow_run.notification` when it has notify states, and the three endings.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `customer_add.additional_contact_ref`, `customer_add.class_ref`, `customer_add.contacts.additional_contact_ref`, `customer_add.currency_ref`, `customer_add.customer_type_ref`, `customer_add.item_sales_tax_ref`, `customer_add.job_type_ref`, `customer_add.parent_ref`, `customer_add.preferred_payment_method_ref`, `customer_add.price_level_ref`, `customer_add.sales_rep_ref`, `customer_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `customer_add.terms_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `customer_add.additional_contact_ref`, `customer_add.class_ref`, `customer_add.contacts.additional_contact_ref`, `customer_add.currency_ref`, `customer_add.customer_type_ref`, `customer_add.item_sales_tax_ref`, `customer_add.job_type_ref`, `customer_add.parent_ref`, `customer_add.preferred_payment_method_ref`, `customer_add.price_level_ref`, `customer_add.sales_rep_ref`, `customer_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `customer_add.terms_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `customer_add.additional_contact_ref`, `customer_add.class_ref`, `customer_add.contacts.additional_contact_ref`, `customer_add.currency_ref`, `customer_add.customer_type_ref`, `customer_add.item_sales_tax_ref`, `customer_add.job_type_ref`, `customer_add.parent_ref`, `customer_add.preferred_payment_method_ref`, `customer_add.price_level_ref`, `customer_add.sales_rep_ref`, `customer_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `customer_add.terms_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

on_conflict.description: For an update: what happens when QuickBooks says the record changed after it was read (a stale edit sequence, 3200). ask (the default) pauses the run with a conflict prompt carrying the diff, which the app answers with overwrite (optionally with different params) or keep; overwrite re-sends with the current edit sequence without asking; fail raises error 3200 with the diff under response.error.conflict for the chart to handle. An update may leave edit_sequence out: the engine reads the record first and fills it in, and that read is the baseline the diff is judged against.

operation.description: A Semantic.Registry id, e.g. customer.query -- or a template that renders to one, such as ${input.find.operation}, checked when the state is entered.

paginate.description: Page through a query's results: the state raises `page` once per page (response.data that page's records, response.page its number from 1, response.more whether more follow), then `success` once every page is in (response.data the page set, response.count and response.pages its size). Only on a single `operation` that supports an iterator; `params` may not also set `iterator` or `max_returned`.

settle.description: Whether a request QuickBooks never answered is settled before the state raises anything: the engine finds out whether it was applied (a list add by its full name, a transaction add by the external_guid it stamps on it, an update by reading the record back, a delete by its id) and raises success as if the answer had arrived, re-sends, or raises error with type unsettled and the candidates when only the app can tell. false raises error with type no_response at once, as a query does when re-sending fails. Either way a no_response carries response.error.reason, why it went unanswered (timed_out or connector_error: it was sent, so QuickBooks may have applied it; rejected: QuickBooks could not read it; withdrawn: the app withdrew it before it was sent; page_expired: a later page never fetched), and, for an add, response.error.external_guid, the GUID it was sent with, so a chart that does its own looking can recognise the record. An add is stamped with a GUID whether settling is on or off.

as.description: The name the current element is bound to under each: each.line when as is line.

each.description: Run the child once per element of this list, one at a time and in order: a template that renders to a list, such as ${input.lines}. An empty list raises success at once with response.data []. At most 200 elements.

input.description: Rendered against this run's context and passed to the child as its input. With `each`, rendered once per element, with each.<as>, each.index and each.count bound.

on_item_error.description: stop: the first child that fails raises error, with the outputs so far in response.data. continue: a failed element leaves null in response.data and an entry in response.errors, and the state still raises success.

workflow.description: The key of another workflow of the same app to run as this step.

data.description: Any JSON, rendered as the state is entered and sent to the app as a workflow_run.notification webhook, to the webhook_url the run was started with (a run of a workflow that can send one is refused without it: 422 webhook_url_required). `response` here is the response of the event that entered the state -- on a paginated query's `page`, that page -- so `${response.data}` sends the page's records; a page set (a paginating query's `success`) cannot be sent. At most 4 MB once encoded. The run waits for the app's 2xx: then the state raises success with response.delivery_id (the same on every retry), response.seq (1, 2, ... in send order for the run) and response.attempts. Delivery is retried for about an hour (10 attempts); if none succeeds, or the data is over 4 MB, it raises error with response.error.type not_delivered or too_large.

name.description: What the app routes on, such as customers_page: the webhook's `name`.

ui.description: Canvas bookkeeping, ignored by the engine. `x`/`y` place the state; `transitions` places the pill drawn for each of its transitions, keyed `"<event>|<index>"` -- the event and the transition's position within it, which is what identifies a transition. Free-form: anything here is presentation, and a chart with no `ui` at all lays itself out.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

listCreditCardCharges_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

is_to_be_printed.description: If `IsToBePrinted` is true, QuickBooks queues the form for later printing. It does not print immediately; printing is still a user action in QuickBooks.

is_pending.description: If IsPending is set to true, the invoice hasn’t been completed. Pending sales might include unpaid orders, estimates, tracked hours that haven’t yet been billed, or sales of back-ordered items.

ref_number.description: RefNumber is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate RefNumber when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

link_type.description: Indicates the nature of the link between the transactions: ltAMTTYPE means the two transactions are linked based on an amount value (for example an invoice linked to a payment). ltQUANTYPE means the two transactions are linked based on a quantity. ref_number.description: RefNumber is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate RefNumber when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

txn_date.description: The date of the invoice. If you leave TxnDate out of an InvoiceAdd message, QuickBooks might prefill it with the date of the invoice that was most recently saved.

txn_id.description: TxnID is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. TxnID values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

applied_amount.description: Amount of a credit that is applied to a customer’s invoice, or amount of a payment that is applied to a particular bill or vendor credit.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. customer_ref.description: CustomerRef identifies a customer or customer job. If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A ClassRef points to one class; if both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

is_active.description: If IsActive is true, this object is currently enabled for use by QuickBooks. The default value is true.

item_desc.description: The description that will appear on a sales form when the item is used.

accounting_preferences.description: Accounting preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

closing_date.description: The company closing date set within the company file. (The QuickBooks Admin can assign a password restricting access to transactions that occurred before this date.)

is_assigning_journal_entry_numbers.description: If true, QuickBooks will automatically assign a number to each journal entry.

is_requiring_accounts.description: If IsRequiringAccounts is true, a transaction can’t be recorded in the user interface unless it is assigned to an account. (However, transactions affected by this preference always require an account to be specified when added through the SDK.)

is_using_account_numbers.description: If true, an account number can be recorded for new accounts. If you include an account number in AccountAdd object when this preference is false, the account number will still be set, but won’t be visible in the user interface.

is_using_audit_trail.description: If true, QuickBooks will log all transaction changes in the audit trail report. If false, QuickBooks logs only the most recent version of each transaction.

is_using_class_tracking.description: If true, QuickBooks will include a “Class” field on all transactions.

current_app_access_rights.description: CurrentAppAccessRights indicates whether auto-login has been allowed, the name of the auto-login user, and whether the application has been granted access to personal (sensitive) data.

automatic_login_user_name.description: If auto-login is allowed for this QuickBooks company file, AutomaticLoginUserName gives the user name that is allowed to use auto-login.

is_automatic_login_allowed.description: If IsAutomaticLoginAllowed is true, then applications can use auto-login to access this QuickBooks company file.

is_personal_data_access_allowed.description: If true, then access is allowed to personal (sensitive) data in this QuickBooks company file.

finance_charge_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set for how finance charges are assessed against customers for late payment. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

annual_interest_rate.description: The interest rate, set by the QuickBooks user, that QuickBooks will use to calculate finance charges. The default value is 0.

calculate_charges_from.description: This preference is set by the QuickBooks user. Unless they change the value within QuickBooks, it will be DueDate.

finance_charge_account_ref.description: Refers to the name of the account used to track finance charges that customers pay. This is usually an income account. In a request, if a FinanceChargeAccountRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

grace_period.description: The number of days before finance charges apply to customers’ overdue invoices. GracePeriod is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of 0.

is_assessing_for_overdue_charges.description: If true, finance charges are assessed on overdue finance charges. This preference is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of false. (Note that laws vary about whether a company can charge interest on overdue interest payments.)

is_marked_to_be_printed.description: If IsMarkedToBePrinted is true, all newly created finance-charge invoices will be marked “To be printed.” (This makes it easier for the QuickBooks user to print a selection of invoices all at once.) This preference is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value within QuickBooks of false. Whether IsMarkedToBePrinted is true or false in the FinanceChargePreferences aggregate, the QuickBooks user can still change this preference for each individual invoice.

min_finance_charge.description: The minimum finance charge that will be applied regardless of the amount overdue. MinFinanceCharge is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of 0.

items_and_inventory_preferences.description: This aggregate contains the current item inventory settings for this company file.

enhanced_inventory_receiving_enabled.description: Indicator whether the enanched inventory receiving is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

fifo_effective_date.description: Date that FIFO (First In, First Out) is used to calculate the value of inventory sold and on-hand for this company file.

fifo_enabled.description: Indicator whether FIFO (First In, First Out) to calculate the value of inventory sold and on-hand is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_barcode_enabled.description: Indicator whether barcode are enabled for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_rsb_enabled.description: Indicator whether the bin tracking is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_build_assembly_enabled.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for build assemblies in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_inventory_adjustment_enab.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for inventory adjustments in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_purchase_transactions_ena.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for purchase transactions in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_sales_transactions_enable.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for sales transactions in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_serial_or_lot_number.description: Indicator on whether the serial or lot number tracking is being tracked for this company file. IsTrackingSerialOrLotNumber may have one of the following values: None [DEFAULT], SerialNumber, LotNumber

jobs_and_estimates_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set about how to handle jobs and estimates. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

is_printing_items_with_zero_amounts.description: If true, line items with zero amounts will print on progress invoices. (IsPrintingItemsWithZeroAmounts isn’t relevant unless IsUsingProgressInvoices is true.)

is_using_estimates.description: If true, this user is set up to create estimates for jobs.

is_using_progress_invoicing.description: If true, the QuickBooks user can create an invoice for only a portion of an estimate.

multi_currency_preferences.description: This aggregate contains the current multi currency settings for this company file.

home_currency_ref.description: The currency that is set as the home currency for this company file. The home currency is normally the currency of the country where the business is physically located. Although a home currency other than US Dollars can be chosen for the home currency, certain QuickBooks convenience features are available only with a home currency of US Dollars, such as the ability to download via a button click in the UI the current exchange rates for all active currencies, which is supported only for home currency of USD–otherwise you’ll have to look up and add the exchange rates yourself. Also, Intuit services such as payroll and online banking won’t be available as these services are only available in US dollars. Currently, once the home currency has been set and used in any transaction, it can’t be changed.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

is_multi_currency_on.description: Indicates whether the multicurrency feature is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on. Currently, once multicurrency is turned on for a company file, it can’t be turned off.

multi_location_inventory_preferences.description: This aggregate contains the current multilocation inventory settings for this company file.

is_multi_location_inventory_available.description: Indicates whether the multilocation inventory feature is available for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_multi_location_inventory_enabled.description: Indicates whether the multilocation inventory feature is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

purchases_and_vendors_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set about how to handle purchases and vendors. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

days_bills_are_due.description: By default, bills are due this many days after receipt.

default_discount_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where vendor discounts are tracked. In a request, if a DefaultDiscountAccountRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

is_automatically_using_discounts.description: If true, QuickBooks will automatically apply available vendor discounts or credits to a bill that is being paid.

is_using_inventory.description: If IsUsingInventory is true, the inventory-related features of QuickBooks are available.

reports_preferences.description: Reporting preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. The preferences returned through the SDK apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

aging_report_basis.description: “AgeFromDueDate” means that the overdue days shown in these reports will begin with the due date on the invoice. “AgeFromTransactionDate” means that the overdue days shown in these reports will begin with the date the transaction was created.

summary_report_basis.description: Indicates whether summary reports use cash-basis or accrual-basis bookkeeping.

sales_and_customers_preferences.description: Sales and customer preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

default_fob.description: Default FOB (site from which invoiced products are shipped).

default_markup.description: Default percentage that an inventory item will be marked up from its cost.

default_ship_method_ref.description: Will be used as the default value in all “Ship Via” fields. (Refers to an item on the ShipMethod list.) If a DefaultShipMethodRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

is_auto_applying_payments.description: If true, a customer’s payment will automatically be applied to the outstanding invoices for that customer, beginning with the oldest invoice.

is_tracking_reimbursed_expenses_as_incom.description: If true, an expense and the customer’s reiumbursement for that expense can be tracked in separate accounts.

price_levels.description: Price levels let you apply custom pricing rules for selected customers. Once assigned, QuickBooks uses those prices automatically on supported sales forms unless explicitly overridden.

is_rounding_sales_price_up.description: If true, amounts are rounded up to nearest whole dollar for fixed percentage price levels (not for per item price levels).

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

createItemReceipt_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_inventory_add.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.class_ref`, `item_inventory_add.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_add.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_add.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_inventory_add.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.class_ref`, `item_inventory_add.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_add.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_add.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_inventory_add.asset_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.class_ref`, `item_inventory_add.cogs_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.income_account_ref`, `item_inventory_add.parent_ref`, `item_inventory_add.pref_vendor_ref`, `item_inventory_add.purchase_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `item_inventory_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

WorkflowChart.description: A workflow is one JSON document: a Harel statechart whose states queue QuickBooks requests, pause for a decision from the calling app, or transform data. Qube.Workflows.Chart.validate/1 is the source of truth; this schema is documentation and a first-pass check.

input.description: What a run accepts. Validated at run start and published as a JSON Schema.

description.description: What this ending means, when its key does not say it already. Optional. Shown on the canvas, in the usage contract and in the guide.

kind.description: success: the run ends completed with this outcome. failure: the run ends failed with this outcome, and a workflow calling this one receives it as an error with response.outcome set.

output.description: Template rendered when the run ends this way, instead of the chart's own `output`. While it renders, `meta.outcome` holds the outcome key.

outcomes.description: Extra ways a run can end, beyond completed and failed. Each is a success (the default: the workflow worked as designed and this is how it ended; the run ends `completed` with this `outcome`) or, with `"kind": "failure"`, a named failure (the run ends `failed` with this `outcome`, and `error` is whatever the transition assigned to `error`, else the description, else `ended with outcome <key>`). A transition may target a declared outcome from anywhere, and no state at any level may use one of these keys.

output.description: Template evaluated against the final context when the run reaches `completed` or an outcome with no `output` of its own. Defaults to ${vars}. While it renders, `meta.outcome` holds the outcome key.

ui.description: Canvas bookkeeping for the chart itself, ignored by the engine: one entry per outcome placing its terminal node, and `transitions` placing the pills of the root's own handlers, keyed "<event>|<index>".

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage, such as which field it did not support.

code.description: QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

createVendorCredit_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage, such as which field it did not support.

code.description: QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_group_add.item_group_line.item_ref`, `item_group_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_group_add.item_group_line.item_ref`, `item_group_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_group_add.item_group_line.item_ref`, `item_group_add.unit_of_measure_set_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A ClassRef points to one class; if both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level ClassRef is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element CreditCardTxnInputInfo” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “CreditCardTxnResultInfo” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq. You should also save this transaction ID and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you are intending to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

txn_date.description: The date of the sales receipt. In some cases, if you leave TxnDate out of an -Add message, QuickBooks will prefill TxnDate with the date of the last-saved transaction of the same type.

item_sales_tax_ref.description: An ItemSalesTax entry represents one tax rate paid to one tax agency. Use it when a transaction needs a single tax calculation. For multi-rate scenarios, use a sales-tax group instead. If both FullName and ListID are provided for ItemSalesTaxRef, ListID is used.

is_to_be_emailed.description: When enabled, QuickBooks validates the customer email at runtime before sending. If no valid email is available, the request fails.

template_ref.description: QuickBooks templates specify how to print certain transactions. A template query returns the names of all templates that have been defined in QuickBooks. A TemplateRef element refers to one of these templates.

ship_date.description: The date when the product was, or will be, shipped.

listGeneralSummaryReports_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

col_id.description: An identifying number that corresponds to the position of this column in the report. The columns are numbered from left to right, starting with 1.

col_type.description: The type of data that this column contains. ColType values are formatted types. (Returned ctPercent values, for example, will have digits after the decimal points, and ctAddr1 values will be strings.)

data_type.description: The data type: IDTYPE, STRTYPE, and so on.

num_col_title_rows.description: The number of rows to allocate for column titles. Although this number is usually 1, with some reports it is 2 or 3. (For an example of column titles that span multiple rows, look at a ProfitAndLossByJob report in QuickBooks.)

num_columns.description: The number of columns in the report.

num_rows.description: The number of rows in the report.

report_basis.description: If ReportBasis is rbCash, the report bases income and expenses on the dates when money changed hands.rbAccrual, the report bases income on the dates when customers were invoiced and bases expenses on the dates when bills were entered.rbNone, the report uses the default ReportBasis, which is either the QuickBooks Preference setting or the QuickBooks default for a given type of report. In a report response, the SDK returns rbNone for reports that don’t support ReportBasis. (The 1099 report, for example, has its own basis for generation.)

report_data.description: If the report contains any data, it is given row-by-row in a ReportData aggregate.

data_row.description:
A data row contains the actual data for each column.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

subtotal_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated subtotal of the data in all the rows since the last SubTotalRow and, usually, a single underline. There can be multiple SubTotalRow aggregates in a report.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

text_row.description:
A text row contains only text and is used mainly for headings.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

total_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated total of all the data that has come before and a double underline. There will only be one TotalRow per report. If TotalRow doesn’t include any numerical values, the columns required to show the total values aren’t part of the report. These columns weren’t included when the report was customized.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

report_title.description: The main title for this report.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. The “override” here refers to the unit within the set, not the UOM Set itself, which you can’t change or override–the UOM set that can be set or changed only in the item itself via an Item Mod request.

quantity.description: On transaction lines, QuickBooks can derive one value from the other two among Quantity, Rate, and Amount. If you supply Quantity and Amount, QuickBooks calculates Rate. If you supply Quantity and Rate, QuickBooks calculates Amount.

service_date.description: Indicates the date on which the QuickBooks user performs the service for the customer.

total_amount.description: Total amount of money paid or received. In a receive payment add transaction that has payment amount elements (such as AppliedToTxnAdd lines) you must supply a TotalAmount and the sum of all the PaymentAmount elements must not be greater than the TotalAmount.

memo.description: Message that appears in reports, but not on the invoice.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example, an inventory item with the FullName of GermanCars:Mercedes-Benz:CL500I99AA might have a parent object with the FullName of GermanCars:Mercedes-Benz. In a request, if a ParentRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

sales_tax_code_ref.description: SalesTaxCodeRef points to the sales-tax code used for an item or customer context. QuickBooks includes default TAX and NON codes, and a code can be deleted only when nothing references it. If sales tax is disabled, QuickBooks assigns the default non-taxable code. If both FullName and ListID are provided in SalesTaxCodeRef, FullName is ignored.

sublevel.description: The number of ancestors. For example, The customer job with Name = carpets and FullName = Jones:Building2:carpets would have a sublevel of 2.

time_modified.description: Time the object was last modified.
