owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

txn_id.description: TxnID is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. TxnID values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

txn_number.description: An identifying number for this transaction.

message.description: QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_discount_mod.account_ref`, `item_discount_mod.class_ref`, `item_discount_mod.parent_ref`, `item_discount_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_discount_mod.account_ref`, `item_discount_mod.class_ref`, `item_discount_mod.parent_ref`, `item_discount_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_discount_mod.account_ref`, `item_discount_mod.class_ref`, `item_discount_mod.parent_ref`, `item_discount_mod.sales_tax_code_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

item_inventory_ref.description: An inventory item is any merchandise or part that a business purchases, tracks as inventory, and then resells. In QuickBooks, information about an inventory item is grouped into three categories:Puchase Information includes PurchaseDesc, PurchaseCost, COGSAccountRef, and PrefVendorRef. Sales Information includes SalesDesc, SalesPrice, and SalesTaxCodeRef. Inventory Information includes AssetAccountRef, ReorderPoint, QuantityOnHand, TotalValue, and InventoryDate. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. An ItemInventoryRef aggregate refers to an inventory item. In a request, if an ItemInventoryRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

cancel_reason.description: Why the run was cancelled, when a reason was given.

current_state.description: Where the run is: the leaf state path, and while a workflow it calls is running, on into that workflow -- `<calling state> / <state in the called workflow>`, such as `create_customer / resolve_conflict.find_holder`. Null once it has ended.

links.description: `self` (this run), `decisions` (answer a question), `cancel` (stop the run) and `ui` (the run in QuBeSync).

outcome.description: How the run ended, once it has. With state completed: completed, or a success the workflow declares (such as cancelled) -- it worked as designed and this is how it ended. With state failed: failed, or a failure the workflow declares (such as customer_over_limit) -- something needs attention, and this names what. Null while the run is still going.

prompt.description: Present while awaiting_input: `id` (the question's id, as the workflow's contract lists it -- its path from this run, `<calling state> / <wait state>`, when a workflow this one calls asked), `kind`, message, data and the options to choose from. `from` is set when a workflow this one calls asked the question: `workflow` (its key) and `state` (its own wait state) -- that workflow runs as part of this run, so answer it here either way. When the asking workflow runs once per item of a list, `from` also carries `item_index` (0-based) and `item_count`. `kind` says who asked: `decision` for a `wait` state's own question, `conflict` when the engine asks about an update that met a stale edit sequence (someone changed the record in QuickBooks after the run read it, error 3200) and the state's `on_conflict` is `ask`, its default. A conflict prompt's `id` is `conflict:<state>` (prefixed like any question when a workflow this one calls asked), `state` is the request state that sent the update, and `data` carries `operation` (the update, e.g. `customer.update`), `sent` (the fields it carries, without its id and edit sequence), `current` (the record QuickBooks has now, with its edit sequence), `as_read` (the record as the run last read it, or null when it never read it), `conflicts` (one `{field, sent, current, as_read}` row per field being updated that someone else changed too) and `theirs` (one `{field, as_read, current}` row per field they changed that the update does not touch; empty when `as_read` is null). Its options are fixed: `overwrite` re-sends with the current edit sequence -- the original fields, or `data.params` (an object, optional) in their place -- and `keep` carries on with the record as QuickBooks has it.

kind.description: decision: a wait state's own question. conflict: the engine asks about an update that met a stale edit sequence; see the prompt's description.

state.description: running means it is working -- a QuickBooks request is in flight, or a workflow it calls is running as part of it; awaiting_input means it needs a decision from you, whichever part of it asked. cancelled means somebody stopped it (`POST .../cancel`); `outcome` stays null and `cancel_reason` says why, when they said.

summary.description: Set once the run has ended (completed, failed or cancelled): what it did. Null while it is going.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow this is a run of. Still set when that workflow has been deleted: the run is kept, readable by its id until retention removes it.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

Applies to: `time_tracking_mod.class_ref`, `time_tracking_mod.customer_ref`, `time_tracking_mod.entity_ref`, `time_tracking_mod.item_service_ref`, `time_tracking_mod.payroll_item_wage_ref`. * `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

`item_line_ret` and `item_group_line_ret` combine: any number of each.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

item_group_ref.description: ItemGroup objects represent items that are grouped together for fast entry, and an ItemGroupRef aggregate refers to one of these item groups. In a request, if an ItemGroupRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored. You can use an ItemGroupQuery request to get information about all the item groups that are set up in the QuickBooks file.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

item_line_ret.description: An ItemLine is used to track any portion of a transaction that represents the purchase of an “item.” If ItemLineAdd doesn’t specify an Amount, Cost, or Quantity, then QuickBooks will calculate Amount based on a Quantity of 1 and the suggested Cost.

billable_status.description: The billing status of this item line or expense line.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A ClassRef points to one class; if both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level ClassRef is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

listSalesTaxReturns_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

WorkflowRunEvent.description: One thing that happened in a run you started, or in a workflow it calls -- which runs as part of it, so its events are in the same stream, right after the `call_started` event that began it. Append-only.

item_index.description: Only inside an element of a state that runs a workflow once per item: which element (0-based).

kind.description: `call_started` and `call_finished` begin and end a workflow this one calls; `run_started` and `run_completed`/`run_failed`/`run_cancelled` with a `state` are that workflow's own start and end, at the calling state. `notification_queued`, `notification_delivered` and `notification_failed` are a notify state's `workflow_run.notification`: sent, answered with a 2xx, or never delivered.

payload.description: What the kind carries: `response` (the whole response) on response_received -- except a paginated query's last one, which has `count` and `pages` in place of `data`, the records being on each page_delivered, `owner`/`event`/`index`/`description`/`target`/`to`/`considered` on transition_taken, `assigned` on assigns_applied, `option`/`data`/`by` on decision_received, `page`/`count`/`queued_request_id`/`response` on page_delivered (a paginated query's page, raised as `page`; `response` is that page's, as on response_received), `workflow` (and `item_index`/`item_count`) on call_started and call_finished, `delivery_id`/`name`/`seq`/`bytes` on notification_queued, notification_delivered (with `attempts`) and notification_failed (with `attempts` and `error`, whose `type` is `not_delivered` or `too_large`; one too large was never sent and has no `seq`) -- never what was sent, and so on. A `response` that succeeded but that QuickBooks warned about has `warning` with its `code` and `message` (530, for one: a field it does not support, which it saved the record without). A `response` that is an error has `error` with `code`, `type` and `message`; when `type` is `no_response` (QuickBooks never answered) it also has `reason`, why: `timed_out` or `connector_error` (sent, so QuickBooks may have applied it), `rejected` (QuickBooks could not read it), `withdrawn` (withdrawn before it was sent) or `page_expired` (a later page never fetched), and, for an add, `external_guid`, the GUID it was sent with. Response bodies are removed 7 days after the run ends.

seq.description: Its position in the stream, which is the order entries come in and what `after` takes: `7` is the run's own 7th event, `7.2` the 2nd event of the workflow the 7th started, `7.3.1` a level deeper.

state.description: Where it happened, as a path from the run you started: `create_customer / try_create` is a state of the workflow `create_customer` calls. Null for what happened to the run as a whole.

vars_after.description: `vars` of the workflow it belongs to once this event had happened. Null 7 days after the run ends.

workflow.description: The key of the workflow whose chart the event belongs to.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

item_inventory_assembly_ref.description: An inventory assembly item is one that is assembled or manufactured from inventory items. The items and/or assemblies that make up the assembly are called components. For Premier, an assembly can have a maximum of 100 components. For Enterprise, the maximum is 500 components.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

item_inventory_ref.description: An inventory item is any merchandise or part that a business purchases, tracks as inventory, and then resells. In QuickBooks, information about an inventory item is grouped into three categories:Puchase Information includes PurchaseDesc, PurchaseCost, COGSAccountRef, and PrefVendorRef. Sales Information includes SalesDesc, SalesPrice, and SalesTaxCodeRef. Inventory Information includes AssetAccountRef, ReorderPoint, QuantityOnHand, TotalValue, and InventoryDate. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. An ItemInventoryRef aggregate refers to an inventory item. In a request, if an ItemInventoryRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

price_level_fixed_percentage.description:
When you create a price level, you must specify whether it is a fixed percentage or a per item price level. Once you create the price level, you can’t change this. QuickBooks Pro and greater versions support fixed percentages, but only QuickBooks Premier and Enterprise support the per item price level. Where is this discount applied if Price Levels are enabled in QuickBooks preferences? The discount is applied to the sales price of the item. If the price level is applied to a customer, it automatically adjusts the Rate and Amount columns for applicable line items in a QuickBooks Sales Order form, Invoice form, etc. for that customer. The QuickBooks user could still select a different price level. However, the customer price level simply establishes a default price. If no price level is applied to the customer, then the QuickBooks user can apply a price level by clicking the dropdown list of price levels that appears next to the Rate column. The default in this case is simply the sales price established for the item. Notice that this value supports both positive and negative values. For example, a value of 20 would increase the price by 20% and value of -10 would decrease the price by 10%.

Choose at most one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item_ret`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (CustomPrice) or a fixed discount percentage (CustomPricePercent). Alternatively, instead of a flat custom price or discount, you could apply a price discount based on either the current custom price, the standard price of the item, or the cost of the item.

Choose exactly one of: `custom_price`, or `custom_price_percent`.

custom_price_percent.description:

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage, such as which field it did not support.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `item_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `item_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `item_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). * `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.

* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

due_date.description: The date on which payment is due.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

Applies to: `sales_order_add.class_ref`, `sales_order_add.customer_msg_ref`, `sales_order_add.customer_ref`, `sales_order_add.customer_sales_tax_code_ref`, `sales_order_add.item_sales_tax_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.class_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.inventory_site_location_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.inventory_site_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.item_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.price_level_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_group_add.inventory_site_location_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_group_add.inventory_site_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_group_add.item_group_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_rep_ref`, `sales_order_add.ship_method_ref`, `sales_order_add.template_ref`, `sales_order_add.terms_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.

Applies to: `sales_order_add.class_ref`, `sales_order_add.customer_msg_ref`, `sales_order_add.customer_ref`, `sales_order_add.customer_sales_tax_code_ref`, `sales_order_add.item_sales_tax_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.class_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.inventory_site_location_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.inventory_site_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.item_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.price_level_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_add.sales_tax_code_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_group_add.inventory_site_location_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_group_add.inventory_site_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_order_line_group_add.item_group_ref`, `sales_order_add.sales_rep_ref`, `sales_order_add.ship_method_ref`, `sales_order_add.template_ref`, `sales_order_add.terms_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.

message.description:

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. name.description: Name is the case-insensitive short name of a list object (without ancestors). It must be unique within its hierarchy scope. Hierarchical lists can reuse the same Name in different branches because FullName remains distinct.

price_level_fixed_percentage.description:
When you create a price level, you must specify whether it is a fixed percentage or a per item price level. Once you create the price level, you can’t change this. QuickBooks Pro and greater versions support fixed percentages, but only QuickBooks Premier and Enterprise support the per item price level. Where is this discount applied if Price Levels are enabled in QuickBooks preferences? The discount is applied to the sales price of the item. If the price level is applied to a customer, it automatically adjusts the Rate and Amount columns for applicable line items in a QuickBooks Sales Order form, Invoice form, etc. for that customer. The QuickBooks user could still select a different price level. However, the customer price level simply establishes a default price. If no price level is applied to the customer, then the QuickBooks user can apply a price level by clicking the dropdown list of price levels that appears next to the Rate column. The default in this case is simply the sales price established for the item. Notice that this value supports both positive and negative values. For example, a value of 20 would increase the price by 20% and value of -10 would decrease the price by 10%.

Choose at most one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item_ret`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

price_level_per_item_ret.description: Choose at most one of: `price_level_fixed_percentage`, or the set (`currency_ref`, `price_level_per_item_ret`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (CustomPrice) or a fixed discount percentage (CustomPricePercent). Alternatively, instead of a flat custom price or discount, you could apply a price discount based on either the current custom price, the standard price of the item, or the cost of the item.

Choose exactly one of: `custom_price`, or `custom_price_percent`.

custom_price_percent.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (CustomPrice) or a fixed discount percentage (CustomPricePercent).

Choose exactly one of: `custom_price`, or `custom_price_percent`.

If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. Use ItemQuery to list available items and types in the company file.

col_id.description: An identifying number that corresponds to the position of this column in the report. The columns are numbered from left to right, starting with 1.

col_type.description: The type of data that this column contains. ColType values are formatted types. (Returned ctPercent values, for example, will have digits after the decimal points, and ctAddr1 values will be strings.)

data_type.description: The data type: IDTYPE, STRTYPE, and so on.

num_col_title_rows.description: The number of rows to allocate for column titles. Although this number is usually 1, with some reports it is 2 or 3. (For an example of column titles that span multiple rows, look at a ProfitAndLossByJob report in QuickBooks.)

num_columns.description: The number of columns in the report.

num_rows.description: The number of rows in the report.

report_basis.description: If ReportBasis is rbCash, the report bases income and expenses on the dates when money changed hands.rbAccrual, the report bases income on the dates when customers were invoiced and bases expenses on the dates when bills were entered.rbNone, the report uses the default ReportBasis, which is either the QuickBooks Preference setting or the QuickBooks default for a given type of report. In a report response, the SDK returns rbNone for reports that don’t support ReportBasis. (The 1099 report, for example, has its own basis for generation.)

report_data.description: If the report contains any data, it is given row-by-row in a ReportData aggregate.

data_row.description:
A data row contains the actual data for each column.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

subtotal_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated subtotal of the data in all the rows since the last SubTotalRow and, usually, a single underline. There can be multiple SubTotalRow aggregates in a report.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

text_row.description:
A text row contains only text and is used mainly for headings.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

total_row.description:
A row that contains a calculated total of all the data that has come before and a double underline. There will only be one TotalRow per report. If TotalRow doesn’t include any numerical values, the columns required to show the total values aren’t part of the report. These columns weren’t included when the report was customized.

`data_row`, `text_row`, `subtotal_row` and `total_row` combine: any number of each.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

report_title.description: The main title for this report.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

txn_id.description: TxnID is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. TxnID values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

txn_number.description: An identifying number for this transaction.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `data_ext_mod.list_obj_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `data_ext_mod.list_obj_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `data_ext_mod.list_obj_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

Applies to: `to_do_add.customer_ref`, `to_do_add.employee_ref`, `to_do_add.lead_ref`, `to_do_add.vendor_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.

* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.

* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

WorkflowChartTemplate.description: Any JSON value. Strings may hold ${...} references; a map may hold the reserved "$from" key, whose rendered map the rest of the map is deep-merged onto. A map holding "$map" is a list built from another: {"$map": "${vars.items}", "as": "item", "template": ...} renders template once per element, with the element at each.<as>, its position at each.index and the length at each.count. {"$add": [a, b, ...]} is the sum of its operands and {"$default": [a, b, ...]} the first candidate that renders to something. {"$merge": [a, b, ...]} deep-merges each object onto the ones before it, as "$from" does (objects merge key by key; lists and scalars replace; an operand that renders to nothing is skipped). {"$find": "${vars.items}", "as": "item", "where": condition} is the first element the condition holds for, with the element at each.<as>, or nothing. No other $-prefixed key is allowed.

$add.description: The sum of its operands: numbers, or templates that render to numbers; nothing counts as 0.

$default.description: The first of its candidates that renders to something other than nothing or an empty string.

$find.description: A template that renders to a list. With "where" (a condition, required) and "as" (default item): the first element for which the condition holds, the element at each.<as>, each.index and each.count; nothing when none does. Only $find, as and where.

$merge.description: Objects, or templates that render to objects, each deep-merged onto the ones before it: objects merge key by key, lists and scalars replace. An operand that renders to nothing is skipped. Alone in its object.

For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `time_tracking_add.class_ref`, `time_tracking_add.customer_ref`, `time_tracking_add.entity_ref`, `time_tracking_add.item_service_ref`, `time_tracking_add.payroll_item_wage_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `time_tracking_add.class_ref`, `time_tracking_add.customer_ref`, `time_tracking_add.entity_ref`, `time_tracking_add.item_service_ref`, `time_tracking_add.payroll_item_wage_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `time_tracking_add.class_ref`, `time_tracking_add.customer_ref`, `time_tracking_add.entity_ref`, `time_tracking_add.item_service_ref`, `time_tracking_add.payroll_item_wage_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.expense_account_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.liability_account_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.payment_template_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.vendor_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.expense_account_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.liability_account_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.payment_template_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.vendor_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.expense_account_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.liability_account_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.payment_template_ref`, `payroll_item_workers_compensation_add.vendor_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

bar_code_value.description: Value of the barcode in the item.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A ClassRef points to one class; if both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level ClassRef is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

deposit_to_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where these funds will be (or have been) deposited. message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element CreditCardTxnInputInfo” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “CreditCardTxnResultInfo” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq. You should also save this transaction ID and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you are intending to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

txn_id.description: TxnID is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. TxnID values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.
