txn_number.description: An identifying number for this transaction.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `name_in_use` (3100): The name is already used by a customer, vendor, employee or other name. QuickBooks requires names to be unique across those lists. Query for the name first, or choose a different one -- the create_customer_safely template does exactly that.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

updateCheck_response_json.description: QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer. Only an `Error` severity from QuickBooks is `status: "error"` (and makes the request's `state` `error`), so a query that matched nothing is still `success`. A `Warn` severity is a `success` with `warning` beside it.

account_ref.description: AccountRef points to an account in the company file. If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. Meaning depends on context: for checks it is the funding account; for ExpenseLineAdd it may be required by accounting preferences; for credit-card transactions it identifies the bank or card account involved. error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

WorkflowRunWebhookPayload.description: The body QuBeSync POSTs to a run's `webhook_url`, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` like every other QuBeSync webhook. One flat envelope for every event, always about the run the app started -- a workflow it calls runs as part of it and sends none of its own. `GET links.run` returns the whole run. `workflow_run.notification` is data a notify state sends the app mid-run: the run waits for a 2xx before it goes on, so notifications arrive one at a time, in `seq` order, all before the run's ending webhook; a failed delivery is retried for about an hour (10 attempts) with the same `delivery_id`.

data.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notify state's `data`, rendered -- any JSON, at most 4 MB.

delivery_id.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notification's id, the same on every retry of it. Deduplicate on it: delivery is at least once.

error.description: Only on `workflow_run.completed`, `workflow_run.failed` and `workflow_run.cancelled`.

from.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: null when the run's own workflow sent it; when a workflow it calls did, which -- `workflow`, its own `state`, and `item_index`/`item_count` inside a state that runs once per item -- as `prompt.from` says. Never a run id: `run_id` is always the run the app started.

links.description: `run` returns the whole run; `decisions` is where to answer; `cancel` stops the run; `ui` opens it in QuBeSync.

name.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notify state's `name`, what the app routes on, such as `customers_page`.

outcome.description: Only on the endings; null on `workflow_run.cancelled`.

prompt.description: Only on `workflow_run.awaiting_input`: the question, exactly as `prompt` on the run -- `id`, `kind`, `message`, `data`, `options`, and `from` (`workflow`, `state`) when a workflow this one calls asked. `kind` is `decision` for a wait state's own question and `conflict` when the engine asks about an update whose record someone changed after the run read it (a stale edit sequence, 3200): then `state` names the request state, `data` carries `operation`, `sent`, `current`, `as_read` (null when the run never read the record), `conflicts` and `theirs`, and the options are always `overwrite` (optionally with `data.params`, the fields to send instead) and `keep`. See `prompt` on WorkflowRun.

kind.description: decision: a wait state's own question. conflict: the engine asks about an update that met a stale edit sequence; see the prompt's description.

seq.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: 1, 2, 3... for the run, in the order its notifications were sent, the workflows it calls included.

state.description: Only on `workflow_run.notification`: the notify state's path from the run, on into a workflow it calls (`sync_page / send_customer`), as a question's `id` is.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; also the `t=` in the signature header.

workflow.description: The workflow's key -- still set after that workflow has been deleted.

workflow_id.description: The workflow's id. Null once that workflow has been deleted -- its runs are kept, run to the end on the version they started with, and still name it in `workflow` -- and for a built-in chart, which has no workflow row.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

amount.description:
A monetary amount.

Choose at most one of: `amount`, or `rate_percent`.

rate_percent.description:
Indicates the price of something as a percent.

Choose at most one of: `amount`, or `rate_percent`.

ship_address.description: This aggregate supports at most five address lines. You can provide a structured address (Addr1-Addr3 plus City/State/PostalCode/etc.) or use block mode (Addr1-Addr5 only). Do not mix block mode with other address fields. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in ShipAddressBlock or BillAddressBlock.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a BillAddress or ShipAddress aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.

item_inventory_ref.description: An inventory item is any merchandise or part that a business purchases, tracks as inventory, and then resells. In QuickBooks, information about an inventory item is grouped into three categories:Puchase Information includes PurchaseDesc, PurchaseCost, COGSAccountRef, and PrefVendorRef. Sales Information includes SalesDesc, SalesPrice, and SalesTaxCodeRef. Inventory Information includes AssetAccountRef, ReorderPoint, QuantityOnHand, TotalValue, and InventoryDate. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. An ItemInventoryRef aggregate refers to an inventory item. In a request, if an ItemInventoryRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

item_group_ref.description: ItemGroup objects represent items that are grouped together for fast entry, and an ItemGroupRef aggregate refers to one of these item groups. In a request, if an ItemGroupRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored. You can use an ItemGroupQuery request to get information about all the item groups that are set up in the QuickBooks file.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

override_uom_set_ref.description: When you modify a transaction line to change the unit of measure used in that line, you use this aggregate to specify the UOM set within which you are choosing an available unit of measure. The “override” here refers to the unit within the set, not the UOM Set itself, which you can’t change or override–the UOM set that can be set or changed only in the item itself via an Item Mod request.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `no_match` (1): The query ran and matched nothing. Not a failure. `data` is an empty list; widen the filter if you expected results.
* `not_found_by_key` (500): A record was looked up by an exact key (a FullName or ListID) and does not exist. Not a failure: you asked whether it exists and the answer is no. Create it, or query more broadly.

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.

A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `sales_tax_payment_check_mod.bank_account_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `sales_tax_payment_check_mod.bank_account_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `sales_tax_payment_check_mod.bank_account_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `cannot_modify` (3170): QuickBooks refused to save the change to an existing record.
* `closing_date_modify` (3171): The transaction is dated on or before the company's closing date, which is password-protected. A QuickBooks admin has to remove the closing-date password (Accounting company preferences) before it can be changed.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `stale_edit_sequence` (3200): The edit_sequence sent is not the record's current one: it changed in QuickBooks after you read it. Query the record for its current edit_sequence, re-apply your change, and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.

message.description:
QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

warning.description: Present only when QuickBooks answered with a `Warn` severity: it carried the request out, and `data` is what it saved or found, but it has something to say about it. For example code `530` with the message `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.` means the record was saved without that field, so an add or update that comes back with a `warning` may not have saved everything it sent. Absent on a plain success and on an error.

code.description:
QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

* `field_not_supported` (530): QuickBooks saved the record but ignored a field it does not support; the message names the field. Not a failure: the record was saved without that field. Leave it out, or keep the information where QuickBooks does store it (a journal entry keeps a memo on each line, not on the entry).

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage, such as which field it did not support.

code.description: QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage.

type.description:
A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

* `unsupported_request` (1030): The QuickBooks this connection talks to does not support this request. Sending it again will not help. On a simulated connection it means the simulator does not model this request yet; its message says so.
* `invalid_object_id` (3000): A ListID or TxnID in the request is not a valid id at all; the message names the field. Applies to: `transfer_inventory_add.from_inventory_site_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.to_inventory_site_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.from_inventory_site_location_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.item_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.to_inventory_site_location_ref`. Send the id exactly as QuickBooks returned it. A well-formed id whose record is gone is 3120 instead.
* `string_too_long` (3070): A text value is longer than QuickBooks allows for that field; the message names the field. Shorten the value and send the request again.
* `object_not_found` (3120): The request named a record by its ListID or TxnID, and the company file has no such record. Applies to: `transfer_inventory_add.from_inventory_site_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.to_inventory_site_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.from_inventory_site_location_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.item_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.to_inventory_site_location_ref`. It may have been deleted or merged in QuickBooks, or the id came from another company file. Look it up again (by name, say) and retry with the id QuickBooks returns.
* `invalid_reference` (3140): A reference names a record the company file does not have; the message says which list (Account, Item, Customer...). Applies to: `transfer_inventory_add.from_inventory_site_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.to_inventory_site_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.from_inventory_site_location_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.item_ref`, `transfer_inventory_add.transfer_inventory_line_add.to_inventory_site_location_ref`. Check the referenced record exists -- query for it -- or create it first. An empty value in the message means the reference was sent blank.
* `missing_element` (3150): QuickBooks requires an element the request left out; the message names it. Add the named field and send the request again.
* `in_use` (3175): The record is in use, so it cannot be added, changed or deleted right now.
* `locked` (3176): Someone has the record open in QuickBooks, or QuickBooks is in a single-user mode (such as the Adjust Quantity/Value on Hand window) that blocks changes. Ask the customer to close that window in QuickBooks, then send the request again.
* `cannot_save` (3180): QuickBooks refused to save the new record; the text after 'QuickBooks error message:' says why. Common causes: a transaction with no lines (or lines with no item), and an item with no posting account. Fix what the message names and send it again.
* `invalid_value` (3210): A field's value is not one QuickBooks accepts; the message names the field and the value.
* `not_authorized` (3220): QuickBooks refused the request: no permission for it, or the feature is turned off in this company file.
* `feature_not_enabled` (3250): The feature is turned off in this company file, or this edition of QuickBooks does not have it.
* `insufficient_permission` (3260): The permission level QuickBooks granted does not allow this action.
* `read_only_access` (3263): The application has read-only access to this company file, so it cannot add or change records. The QuickBooks administrator has to grant the application read/write access.
* `missing_posting_account` (3270): QuickBooks needs an account to post this to, and none was given or defaulted.

apiKey.description: Use your app's API key as the username, and leave the password blank

info.description:
A single generic operation surface for every curated qbXML request QuBe Sync supports, driven directly off the qbXML schema -- see the [MCP server](/mcp-server) to explore available operations interactively.

**Every endpoint queues a request and returns it immediately (`201`, a `QueuedRequest`).** QuickBooks Desktop is reached through the customer's Web Connector, which polls QuBe Sync, so the answer arrives seconds to minutes later. **Pass a `webhook_url` with every request**: when QuickBooks has answered, QuBe Sync POSTs the same document to it -- `state` set, `response_json` filled in -- signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (see the Webhooks guide). `response_json` is the `{status, data}` envelope documented on each operation: `status: "success"` with `data` derived from the qbXML `*Ret` (and `warning`, QuickBooks' code and message, when it carried the request out but warned about it), or `status: "error"` with QuickBooks' own status code and message -- a QuickBooks business error is a *successful* HTTP round trip. `links.self` returns the request on demand (for a dashboard, a retry, a script); it is not the integration path.

Authentication is HTTP Basic with your app's API key as the username and a blank password. Connections themselves (creating one, onboarding, its QWC file and password) are the `/connections` endpoints; every QuickBooks operation is scoped to one of them.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. get.description:
qbXML: `AccountQueryRq`.

AccountQuery is a list query that returns data for all accounts that match the provided filter criteria. Notice that it returns only data internal to the account itself. It doesn’t return any data about transactions involving the account. It does, however, return the parent account, if there is one. You can search across all accounts or you can specify an account type and search only those.

If you are querying for an account whose FullName contains a number, the query might return an account that has a matching account number rather than a matching FullName. For example, if you are querying for an account named 12345, and 12345 happens to be the account number of a totally different account, the query won’t return what you asked for (the account named 12345), but instead will return the account with the account number 12345.

This problem won’t happen if:

- the “show account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, or
- the account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.)

To avoid this problem:

- Don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number.
- If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 12345a.

post.description:
qbXML: `AccountAddRq`. The `account_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

This message allows you to perform the same activities as a user does in the QB New Account form, which can be accessed in QB by selecting Lists->Chart of Accounts->Accounts->New. If you want the account to be a subaccount to an existing account, similar to using the SubAccount checkbox and selection list drop down in the New Account form, you use the ParentRef aggregate. Notice that the ParentRef can take either the parent account’s ListID or FullName. It is important to note that the parent account specified in the ParentRef must have the same account type (AccountType) of the child account that you are creating. (The AccountType field maps to the Type pulldown menu in the New Accounts field.) The AccountNumber is NOT the account number assigned by your bank or other entity. (That number is specified in the BankNumber field.) The account number is simply part of a numbering scheme used by accounting systems to help provide a visual hierarchy and ordering of all of the accounts in a Chart of Accounts. QuickBooks provides this functionality for those who need or want it, but by default has this functionality turned off. The AccountNumber field maps to the Number field in the New Account form, which appears only if the Accounting preferences for the company have been set to use account numbering. By default, account numbers aren’t used. In the SDK, you can set the account numbers if you want, even if the preference for it has been turned off. The numbers would then appear later if the user turned this preference on. In the OpenBalance field for certain types of new Accounts, you may want to leave the opening balance at 0 if you are going to fund the account from another account. That process will effectively create the opening balance. How do you increase and decrease amounts in bank accounts? The following requests increase the balance in a bank account: Deposit Add ReceivePaymentAdd Journal Entry Add Sales ReceiptAdd The following requests decrease the balance in a bank account: CheckAdd Bill PaymentCheckAdd JournalEntryAdd

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.

Retrieves the specified credit card refund transaction or transactions.

parameters.description: The connection (a customer's QuickBooks company file) this request is queued for.
parameters.name: connection_id

parameters.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.
parameters.name: request_id

parameters.description: Use the metaData attribute to control whether query responses include counts. Options are NoMetaData (default), MetaDataOnly (count only), and MetaDataAndResponseData (count plus objects). Counts are approximate and may vary slightly if records are created or deleted during processing.
parameters.name: meta_data

parameters.description: Page through every result: QuBe Sync asks QuickBooks for each page in turn and sends each to your `webhook_url` as it arrives, all with the same `id`. `max_returned` is the page size (100 if you leave it out). It pages a filtered query only: with `ref_number`, `ref_number_case_sensitive` or `txn_id` every match comes back in one answer, so leave `iterator` out.
parameters.name: iterator

parameters.description:
Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: Don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: account_filter

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

note.description: In a BillAddress or ShipAddress aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element CreditCardTxnInputInfo” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “CreditCardTxnResultInfo” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

get.description:
qbXML: `BillPaymentCheckQueryRq`, from qbXML 2.0.

Provides functionality found in the Find/Advanced Find window to find bill payments paid by check. The Find/Advanced Find windows can be reached by clicking the Find button on the main QuickBooks menubar, by selecting Edit->Find, or simply by using the shortcut CTRL-F. Notice that you can use the metaData attribute inside the query tag if you want only a count of the bill payments that will be returned from the query.

If you know the bill payment transaction ID or reference number, you could use these, or search by transaction date, or search by the date where the bill was last modified.

If you need additional filters, you can use the entity filter to search for bills from a specific vendor or vendor sub (using the ListIDWithChildren or FullNameWithChildren tags). You can also search for bills entered against a particular account (the APAccountRef specified in the originating BillAdd request). You can specify all subaccounts by using the various \*WithChildren tags. For example, to find all bills entered against Checking where you have multiple checking accounts, you would use the ListIDWithChildren or FullNameWithChildren tags inside your AccountFilter tags. Finally, you can filter on the RefNumber or RefNumber range. Notice that all of these filters can be used together (ANDed) if desired.

To prevent the return of too much data, you can use MaxReturned to limit the total number of bills returned from the query. In addition, you can limit the type of data that is returned for each bill, using IncludeRetElement. Finally, you can specify whether each bill contains line items using the IncludeLineItems, which by default is False (no line item data).

A BillPaymentCheckAdd request must include either PaymentAmount, SetCredit, or DiscountAmount (or more than one of these). If none of these three is included, the SDK will return an error.

BillPaymentCheckAdd provides the functionality found in the Pay Bills form in the QuickBooks UI. You can reach this form by selecting Retail->Pay Bills from the main QuickBooks menubar. BillPayment is described in detail in the chapter on handling receive payment and bill payment in the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide. Notice that the request requires one (but not more than one!) BillPaymentCheckAdd sub aggregate, which is provided to support the SDK macro feature in this request. (See the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide ([PDF](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/logged-in-content/QBSDK_ProGuide.pdf), 9.6 MB) for more information about macros.) Notice that you can supply only one of these sub aggregates in the request. If you want to pay multiple bills, you must issue a separate request for each bill pay.

If you are using more than one A/P account, make sure that the APAccountRef in the BillPaymentCheckAdd matches the APAccountRef that was used when the Bill was originally added. That is, the Bill was entered in a particular account payable: use that same account payable when you pay the bill using this request.

Notice that although you can set the IsToBePrinted flag, you can’t print checks using the SDK.

Notice that you set the check number, if desired, using the RefNumber tags.

put.description:
qbXML: `BillPaymentCheckModRq`, from qbXML 6.0. The `bill_payment_check_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Note: the AppliedToTxnMod aggregate needs both the TxnID and the payment amount if you aren’t using the SetCredit sub-aggregate or QuickBooks won’t have an amount to apply. If you are using the SetCredit sub-aggregate, you’ll need to set the amount in the AppliedAmount field.

Generally, this is what you can do with BillPaymentCheckMod:

- Modify or clear the RefNumber or Memo.
- Modify (not clear) the TxnDate.
- Modify (not clear) the BankAccountRef
- Modify (not clear) the IsToBePrinted flag.
- For a bill payment check transaction that has been applied to several existing bills, redistribute the payment amounts applied to the bills.
- Change the discount amount applied to particular bill.
- You CANNOT change the credit amount applied to a particular bill. NOT SUPPORTED!
- Apply the payment amount to a different bill. Apply a discount, and a credit. The existing distribution is cleared, except for any credit that may have been applied.
- Use a BillPaymentCheckMod to simply apply an additional credit to a bill. Additional payment amount is available as a credit

Other things you need to know:

When a BillPaymentCheckMod request is processed, if the AppliedToTxnMod aggregate is specified, then the existing payments and discounts will be cleared (but not the credits). The original payment amount will be redistributed according to the AppliedToTxnMod aggregates (0 or more) contained in the BillPaymentCheckMod request. The AppliedToTxnMod aggregate may specify discounts, just as does the AppliedToTxnAdd aggregate. These discounts will replace any original discounts. Credits may also be specified. But if so, then the credits will be additional credits, and won’t affect any credits that were originally applied. The existing payments and discounts will be cleared only if AppliedToTxnMod is specified in the request. This will allow clients to modify other information without modifying the distribution of the payment.

In summary, in the BillPaymentCheckMod request, in the AppliedToTxnMod aggregate, discounts replace those given in the original payment. However credits simply add to any credits that may have been applied before.

qbXML: `BillPaymentCreditCardQueryRq`, from qbXML 2.0.

Provides functionality found in the Find/Advanced Find window to find bill payments that were paid by credit card. The Find/Advanced Find windows can be reached by clicking the Find button on the main QuickBooks menubar, by selecting Edit->Find, or simply by using the shortcut CTRL-F. Notice that you can use the metaData attribute inside the query tag if you want only a count of the bill payments that will be returned from the query.

If you know the bill’s transaction ID or reference number, you could use these, or search by transaction date, or search by the date where the bill was last modified.

Important:

If you made a bill payment by credit card, and ONLY applied a credit using SetCredit (no funds were applied other than the credit), then that payment won’t be returned in this query because it isn’t considered a separate transaction and has no TxnID. To get that kind of payment, you must do a BillQuery on the original bill and specify IncludeLinkedTxns. Any applied credit will be linked directly to the bill.

If you need additional filters, you can use the entity filter to search for bills from a specific vendor or vendor sub (using the ListIDWithChildren or FullNameWithChildren tags). You can also search for bills entered against a particular account (the APAccountRef specified in the originating BillAdd request). You can specify all subaccounts by using the various \*WithChildren tags. For example, to find all bills entered against Checking where you have multiple checking accounts, you would use the ListIDWithChildren or FullNameWithChildren tags inside your AccountFilter tags. Finally, you can filter on the RefNumber or RefNumber range. Notice that all of these filters can be used together (ANDed) if desired.

To prevent the return of too much data, you can use MaxReturned to limit the total number of bills returned from the query. In addition, you can limit the type of data that is returned for each bill, using IncludeRetElement. Finally, you can specify whether each bill contains line items using the IncludeLineItems, which by default is False (no line item data).

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

qbXML: `BillPaymentCreditCardAddRq`, from qbXML 2.0. The `bill_payment_credit_card_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

A BillPaymentCreditCardAdd request must include either PaymentAmount, SetCredit, or DiscountAmount (or more than one of these). If none of these three is included, the SDK will return an error.

BillPaymentCreditCardAdd provides functionality found in the Pay Bills form in the QuickBooks UI. You can reach this form by selecting Retail->Pay Bills from the main QuickBooks menubar. BillPayment is described in detail in the chapter on handling receive payment and bill payment in the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide. Notice that the request requires one (but not more than one!) BillPaymentCreditCardAdd sub aggregate, which is provided to support the SDK macro feature in this request. (See the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide ([PDF](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/logged-in-content/QBSDK_ProGuide.pdf), 9.6 MB) for more information about macros.) Notice that you can supply only one of these sub aggregates in the request. If you want to pay multiple bills, you must issue a separate request for each bill pay.

If you are using more than one A/P account, make sure that the APAccountRef in the BillPaymentCreditCardAdd matches the APAccountRef that was used when the Bill was originally added. That is, the Bill was entered in a particular account payable: use that same account payable when you pay the bill using this request. Notice that although you can set the IsToBePrinted flag, you can’t print checks using the SDK.

Finally, notice that it is possible to issue this request using only SetCredit to apply an existing credit to the bill. However, if you do this, you should be aware that no transaction ID is generated. The credit and the bill simply are linked. See the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide ([PDF](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/logged-in-content/QBSDK_ProGuide.pdf), 9.6 MB) for details.

Adds a billing rate to the billing rate level list. After a billing rate is created, it can be assigned to an employee or vendor (VendorAdd/Mod, EmployeeAdd/Mod) via the BillingRateRef element in the appropriate request. Then, once the billing rate is assigned to an employee or vendor, if you use that employee or vendor in a time transaction (TimeTrackingAdd), then the billing rate will override the rate specified by the service item used in the time transaction.

Use FixedBillingRate to override all service items with a fixed rate. Use BillingRatePerItem to override a specific service item. If you want to specify more than one service item, you’ll need to use one BillingRatePerItem aggregate for each service item.

fixed_billing_rate.description: You use FixedBillingRate if you want the rate to override all service items rates. Consequently, there is no need to specify any service items (and in fact you can’t specify them) if you use this element.

adjust_billing_rate_relative_to.description:
Specifies the service item rate that AdjustPercentage is applied to. Normally, this is set to StandardRate.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_rate`, `custom_rate_percent`), or the set (`adjust_billing_rate_relative_to`, `adjust_percentage`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

adjust_percentage.description:
If you don’t want to apply a custom price (for price levels) or custom rate (for billing rates), you can apply an adjusted price discount using the pair of fields AdjustPercentage and AdjustRelativeTo (AdjustBillingRateRelativeTo for billing rates). You specify the percentage discount or increase in the AdjustPercentage field and the price/rate to be discounted (standard item price, item cost, or the item’s current custom price) in the AdjustRelativeTo fieldTo field. Notice that this value supports both positive and negative values. For example, a value of 20 would increase the price by 20% and value of -10 would decrease the price by 10%.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_rate`, `custom_rate_percent`), or the set (`adjust_billing_rate_relative_to`, `adjust_percentage`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_rate.description:
The value specified here overrides the rate of the service item referenced in this aggregate (in the ItemRef) with the rate you specify here. If instead you wanted a rate that is a percentage higher or lower than the service item rate, you wouldn’t use CustomRate, but you would use AdjustPercentage and AdjustBillingRateRelativeTo.

If you attempt to set the Billing Rate to a percentage for a service item that has an amount for the Rate, you will get an error. The kind of rate you have on the service item determines the kind of billing rate you may have on that item.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_rate`, `custom_rate_percent`), or the set (`adjust_billing_rate_relative_to`, `adjust_percentage`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

item_ref.description: ItemRef may accept all item types or a restricted subset, depending on the request. full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. get.description:
qbXML: `BillQueryRq`.

Provides functionality found in the Find/Advanced Find window to find bills that are to be paid by check. The Find/Advanced Find windows can be reached by clicking the Find button on the main QuickBooks menubar, by selecting Edit->Find, or simply by using the shortcut CTRL-F. Notice that you can use the metaData attribute inside the query tag if you want only a count of the bills that will be returned from the query.

If you know the bill’s transaction ID or reference number, you could use these, or search by transaction date, or search by the date where the bill was last modified. You can search for paid/unpaid bills by using the PaidStatus flag.

If you need additional filters, you can use the entity filter to search for bills from a specific vendor or vendor sub (using the ListIDWithChildren or FullNameWithChildren tags). You can also search for bills entered against a particular account (the APAccountRef specified in the originating BillAdd request). You can specify all subaccounts by using the various \*WithChildren tags. For example, to find all bills entered against Checking where you have multiple checking accounts, you would use the ListIDWithChildren or FullNameWithChildren tags inside your AccountFilter tags. You can filter on the RefNumber or RefNumber range. Notice that all of these filters can be used together (ANDed) if desired.

If you want bill line items returned from the query, you must use the IncludeLineItems tag. Notice that you don’t specify line item groups. If line item groups were set up for the line items, the returned line items are automatically segregated by group.

You can get all of the linked transactions such as PurchaseOrders and Credits by using the IncludeLinkedTxns tag. You can get public data extensions (these are custom data whose fields can be displayed in QuickBooks) by supplying the OwnerID tag set to 0. To get private data extensions (custom data not displayable in QuickBooks) you must use the OwnerID tag set to the known GUID value. You must know the GUID value in order to access private data extensions.

To prevent the return of too much data, you can use MaxReturned to limit the total number of bills returned from the query. In addition, you can limit the type of data that is returned for each bill, using IncludeRetElement. Finally, you can specify whether each bill contains line items using the IncludeLineItems, which by default is False (no line item data).
