201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

put.description:
qbXML: `CreditCardChargeModRq`, from qbXML 6.0. The `credit_card_charge_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

The Credit Card charge mod request allows you to modify an existing credit card charge transaction using the SDK. You can modify most of the fields that can be modified in the QuickBooks UI. That is, this request can be used to modify Purchased from, date, credit card and modify lines from the item table and the expense table.

The following list describes what you can and can’t due with this request:

- You can modify or clear the following fields: Ref Num and Memo
- You can modify (not clear) transaction date
- You can change the credit card account to support the scenario where the credit card transaction was created and posted to the wrong credit card account (impacts your accounting).
- You can modify the Purchase from field (Payee Name) to change the Payee Name on the credit card transaction to a different name (employee, job, customer, vendor, other name). This field can’t be cleared since it is required by QB business logic
- You can’t modify the amount due directly! (However the amount due will change when you modify the transaction lines.)
- You can’t change a Charge to a Credit.
- You can’t Void the charge. Use TxnVoid instead.
- You can clear the entire expense table or the entire item table, but you can’t clear both tables at the same time.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). * `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

put.description:
qbXML: `CreditCardCreditModRq`, from qbXML 6.0. The `credit_card_credit_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

The Credit Card credit mod request allows you to modify an existing credit card credit transaction using the SDK. You can modify most of the fields that can be modified in the QuickBooks UI. That is, this request can be used to modify Purchased from, date, credit card and modify lines from the item table and the expense table.

The following list describes what you can and can’t due with this request:

- You can modify or clear the following fields: Ref Num and Memo
- You can modify (not clear) transaction date
- You can change the credit card account to support the scenario where the credit card transaction was created and posted to the wrong credit card account (impacts your accounting).
- You can modify the Purchase from field (Payee Name) to change the Payee Name on the credit card transaction to a different name (employee, job, customer, vendor, other name). This field can’t be cleared since it is required by QB business logic
- You can’t modify the amount due directly! (However the amount due will change when you modify the transaction lines.)
- You can’t change a Credit to a Charge.
- You can’t Void the credit. Use TxnVoid instead.
- You can clear the entire expense table or the entire item table, but you can’t clear both tables at the same time.

It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

parameters.description:
Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: Don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: account_filter

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.
parameters.name: webhook_url

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

post.description:
qbXML: `CreditMemoAddRq`. The `credit_memo_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds a credit memo. A credit memo specifies an amount that you owe your customer for some reason, such as overpayment against an invoice, returned merchandise, or for some pre-payment. It reduces a customer’s outstanding balance. The CreditMemo doesn’t actually get applied until is referenced in a ReceivePayment transaction inside the SetCredit aggregate.

The CreditMemo shouldn’t be confused with a VendorCredit, which specifies an amount that a vendor owes you.

Using Credit Memos for Pre-Payments

Occasionally an application will need to record pre-payments for a job that is invoiced or paid for only when it is complete. One can create sales receipts for pre-payments using an item other charge named something like “Pre-payment”. If the customer will eventually be sent an invoice for the total job, create credit memos for that customer for the pre-payment amount on each sales receipt. If the customer will be paying for the final job when it is completed and will be issued a sales receipt, don’t create the credit memos. The credit memos are only used for invoice transactions.

When the work order is complete add the invoice to QuickBooks and then apply the credit memos with a ReceivePaymentAdd request. The amount due on the invoice will be reduced properly and all of the transactions will be properly recorded in QuickBooks.

If a sales receipt will be issued at the end of the job, include pre-payment information in multiple lines or as a summary line. Use the description field to list the existing pre-payment sales receipt or receipts so all transactions can be tied together on the final sales receipt.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

qbXML: `CreditMemoModRq`, from qbXML 3.0. The `credit_memo_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Some fields in a CreditMemoMod request can’t be cleared. If any of the following fields is included in a credit-memo modify request, it must contain a value:

- CustomerRef
- ARAccountRef
- TemplateRef
- TxnDate
- IsPending
- DueDate
- ShipDate
- ItemSalesTaxRef
- IsToBePrinted

Within CreditMemoLineMod or CreditMemoLineGroupMod:

- ItemRef
- Quantity
- Rate
- Amount
- SalesTaxCodeRef
- OverrideItemAccountRef

(For more details about what it means for a field to be clearable or not clearable, see [Modify, delete, and void requests and responses](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/develop/exploring-the-quickbooks-desktop-sdk).)

parameters.description: The connection (a customer's QuickBooks company file) this request is queued for.
parameters.name: connection_id

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.
parameters.name: webhook_url

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

bill_address.description: This aggregate supports at most five address lines. You can provide a structured address (Addr1-Addr3 plus City/State/PostalCode/etc.) or use block mode (Addr1-Addr5 only). Do not mix block mode with other address fields. In block mode, each Addr line prints as its own line and is returned in ShipAddressBlock or BillAddressBlock.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a BillAddress or ShipAddress aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

due_date.description: The date on which payment is due.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

exchange_rate.description: ExchangeRate is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. You can supply a rate when adding transactions, but QuickBooks does not provide rates through the SDK. If your home currency is USD and internet access is available, rates can be downloaded in the QuickBooks UI via Lists > Currency > Activities > Download Latest Exchange Rates.

fob.description: QuickBooks uses the term FOB, “freight on board,” to indicate the place from which the product is shipped. The FOB has no accounting implications.

is_pending.description: If IsPending is set to true, the credit memo hasn’t been completed. Within QuickBooks, you can change the IsPending status for a credit memo by choosing “Mark Credit Memo As Pending” or “Mark Credit Memo As Final” from the Edit menu.

is_tax_included.description: For future use with international versions of QuickBooks.

is_to_be_emailed.description: When enabled, QuickBooks validates the customer email at runtime before sending. If no valid email is available, the request fails.

is_to_be_printed.description: If `IsToBePrinted` is true, QuickBooks queues the form for later printing. It does not print immediately; printing is still a user action in QuickBooks.

item_sales_tax_ref.description: An ItemSalesTax entry represents one tax rate paid to one tax agency. Use it when a transaction needs a single tax calculation. For multi-rate scenarios, use a sales-tax group instead. If both FullName and ListID are provided for ItemSalesTaxRef, ListID is used.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

memo.description: The memo doesn’t print on the credit memo, but does appear in the account register and the customer register.

other.description: Other, Other1, and Other2 are built-in transaction custom fields. Other is transaction-level; Other1 and Other2 are line-level. These fields are always available through the SDK and do not require DataExtDef setup. Template labels in the UI can be renamed, but SDK names remain fixed as Other, Other1, and Other2.

ref_number.description: RefNumber is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate RefNumber when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

sales_rep_ref.description: A sales representative must be on the Employee, Vendor, or Other Names list within QuickBooks. Sales representative’s names and initials appear on the Rep drop-down list on QuickBooks sales forms. A SalesRepRef refers to a person on the SalesRep list. In a request, if a SalesRepRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

qbXML: `CurrencyAddRq`, from qbXML 8.0. The `currency_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Creates a user defined currency with the specified name and currency code, both of which will show up in the QuickBooks UI.

Currencies created by users, whether via the UI or via SDK using this request, are distinguished from the built-in QB currencies in the Currency Ret object: they are identified as user defined. User defined currencies don’t get their exchange rates updated automatically by QuickBooks via the Download Current Exchange Rates feature. You’ll always need to manually update the exchange rates. However, other than this, these type of currencies function within QB in the same way as the built-in currencies.

If you haven’t used a user defined currency in a transaction, you can delete it using ListDel. You can’t delete the built-in QB currencies.

decimal_separator.description: This enumerated value controls the display of the decimal point, for example, 1.00 or 1,00. The default is Period but you could alternatively specify a value of Comma.

thousand_separator.description: This enumerated value controls how the thousandth’s place is separated from the next thousand, for example, 1,000,000. The default is Comma, as shown, but you can replace this with one of these values: Period, Space, Apostrophe .

thousand_separator_grouping.description: This enumerated value controls how the display of the currency value is grouped, for example, 10,000,000. The default is XX_XXX_XXX but you could replace this with X_XX_XX_XXX

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

get.description:
qbXML: `DataEventRecoveryInfoQueryRq`, from qbXML 3.0.

You can use the DataEventRecoveryInfoQuery request to find out whether data event recovery information exists for the given subscriber. If it does, then data events have been lost and need to be recovered. (Note that there will be no data event recovery information to return if TrackLostEvents was “tleNone” in the subscriber’s DataEventSubscriptionAdd request.)

Returned data event recovery information currently consists only of DataEventRecoveryTime. For more details about the event-notification feature, see [Subscribing to events and processing event notifications](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/develop/tutorials/subscribing-to-events-and-processing-event-notifications).

qbXML: `DataExtDefAddRq`, from qbXML 2.0. The `data_ext_def_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

This request adds a data extension definition to the specified object type (e.g. Customer) so that extension data can be written to a particular object of that type (e.g., this customer, John Smith. A data extension definition must be created before data can be written to the data extension.

Notice that a custom field data extension definition can be created either by using DataExtDefAdd or via the QuickBooks UI by the user specifying a custom field for an object. Only custom fields can be defined through the UI, however, not private data extensions.

Via the SDK, you create a custom field definition by setting the OwnerID to 0. You create a private data definition by setting OwnerID to a GUID that only your application owns or shares with other applications. Custom fields are available and visible within the QuickBooks UI, whereas private data extensions are seen and used only by your own application or other applications that know the OwnerID GUID.

Data is written to custom fields either via the SDK DataExtAdd/Mod requests or via the QuickBooks UI directly by the end user. Data is written to private data extensions only via the SDK DataExtAdd/Mod requests. You should be careful not to use private data extensions in transaction line items because queries won’t return that private data (use only custom fields on transaction line items).

Notice that creating a custom field data extension definition for Customer and Item causes an automatic propagation of that definition to certain transaction objects. See “AssignToObject” for more details. A full description of this behavior and its usefulness is provided in the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide. DataExtDefAdd doesn’t cause any events to be generated.

qbXML: `DataExtDefDelRq`, from qbXML 2.0.

Deletes the private data extension definition specified by OwnerID and DataExtName. This delete will be successful only for private data extensions.

You can’t use this to delete any custom field definition, whether the custom field was created by the user via the QB UI or via the SDK DataExtDefAdd request.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

post.description:
qbXML: `DataExtAddRq`, from qbXML 2.0. The `data_ext_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Writes data to one data extension. This request can only be invoked if a data extension definition has already been defined for the target object type. That is, before you can perform the DataExtAdd on a particular customer, say John Henry, the data extension must already be defined for the Customer object. Notice that a data extension definition can be defined in either of two ways: via DataExtDefAdd as already described, or via the QuickBooks UI by the user specifying a custom field. Only custom fields can be defined through the UI, not private data extensions.

DataExtAdd adds a custom field (if OwnerID is set to 0) or a private data extension (if OwnerID is set to a GUID) containing the specified value. The custom field or private data extension and value is added to the specified list object, or transaction, or transaction line item.

DataExtAdd will return error 3180 if you invoke this on a custom data ext definition that has been deleted and then re-added from the UI. (You can’t re-add a deleted data ext def via the SDK.) However, you can use DataExtMod to write data to that re-added data ext def.

Important: If you want to perform a DataExtAdd on a transaction line item, you should use custom fields instead of private data extensions because only custom field data will be returned in queries. Currently, private data isn’t returned.

Both DataExtAdd and DataExtMod cause a Modify event to be generated for the parent object. For example invoking one of these on a Customer causes a Customer Modify event. The Time Modified value for that parent object is also updated.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

get.description:
qbXML: `EmployeeQueryRq`.

Returns employee data. Notice that prior to qbXML spec 4.0, an EmployeeQueryRq would return a permissions error if the currently logged in QuickBooks user didn’t have “Payroll and Employees” permission. This would occur even if you only needed data that wasn’t restricted.

However, because of IncludeRetElement (beginning with qbXML spec 4.0), the situation has changed somewhat. You can use that new element to specify fields in the EmployeeRet object that don’t require “Payroll and Employees” permissions. Such a query would return the unrestricted data (such as Name) from an EmployeeQueryRq even if the logged in user lacks “Payroll and Employees” permissions.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. get.description:
qbXML: `EntityQueryRq`.

Queries for the specified entity or entities. A QuickBooks “entity” is a customer, vendor, employee, or person on the QuickBooks “other names” list. Special cases to note:

- In a BillToPayQuery message, EntityRef refers to the vendor name.
- In JournalCreditLine and JournalDebitLine messages for A/R accounts, EntityRef must refer to a customer, or else the transaction won’t be recorded. For A/P accounts the EntityRef must refer to a vendor, or else the transaction won’t be recorded.
- In a *TimeTracking* message, EntityRef can’t refer to a customer, only to an employee, vendor, or person on the “other names” list whose time is being tracked.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else.
