201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

get.description:
qbXML: `PayrollDetailReportQueryRq`, from qbXML 3.0.

Returns information from any of five QuickBooks payroll reports:

- Employee state taxes detail report
- Payroll item detail report (lists the payroll transactions on which each payroll item appears)
- Payroll detail review report (provides detailed information about how QuickBooks calculates tax amounts on employee paychecks and in year-to-date transactions)
- Payroll transaction detail report (shows the line-item detail that appears on each payroll transaction)
- Payroll transactions by payee report (lists payroll transactions, grouping them by payee)

Payroll Summary Reports can be generated if your application is accessing a company file that is currently signed up for a subscription to a payroll service. (If your application isn’t signed up, it will receive an error when it attempts to generate a report in this category.)

The restrictions noted above about payroll reports requiring the use of the Intuit Payroll service don’t apply to the QuickBooks sample companies. You can still test out these reports on the sample companies without subscribing to the payroll service. For all other companies, however, the company must be subscribed.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. * `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. get.description:
qbXML: `PayrollSummaryReportQueryRq`, from qbXML 3.0.

This report returns information from any of three QuickBooks payroll reports:

- Payroll summary report This report shows the total wages, taxes withheld, deductions from net pay, additions to net pay, and employer-paid taxes and contributions for each employee on the payroll.
- Employee earnings summary report This report shows information similar to the payroll summary report, but in a different layout. The report has a row for each employee and a column for each payroll item.
- Payroll liability balances report This report lists the payroll liabilities the QuickBooks company owes to various agencies, such as the federal government, your state government, insurance plan administrators, labor unions, etc. The report covers unpaid liabilities incurred during the period of time shown in the From and To fields. If the company paid a liability incurred within the date range of the report, the report omits that liability, even if the payment occurred after the ending date of the report.

Payroll Summary Reports can be generated if your application is accessing a company file that is currently signed up for a subscription to a payroll service. (If your application isn’t signed up, it will receive an error when it attempts to generate a report in this category.)

The restrictions noted above about payroll reports requiring the use of the Intuit Payroll service don’t apply to the QuickBooks sample companies. You can still test out these reports on the sample companies without subscribing to the payroll service. For all other companies, however, the company must be subscribed.

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.
parameters.name: webhook_url

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

post.description:
qbXML: `PriceLevelAddRq`, from qbXML 4.0. The `price_level_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds a price level. You can use price levels to specify custom pricing for specific customers. Once you create a price level for a customer, QuickBooks will automatically use the custom price in new invoices, sales receipts, sales orders or credit memos for that customer. You can override this automatic feature, however, when you create the invoices, sales receipts, etc.) The user can now specify a price level on line items in the following supported sales transactions: invoices, sales receipts, credit memos, and sales orders. Notice that the response data for the affected sales transaction doesn’t list the price level that was used. The response simply lists the Rate for the item, which was set using the price level. The CurrencyRef should only be used with “per item” price levels.

parameters.description: The connection (a customer's QuickBooks company file) this request is queued for.
parameters.name: connection_id

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.

price_level_fixed_percentage.description: When you create a price level, you must specify whether it is a fixed percentage or a per item price level. Once you create the price level, you can’t change this. QuickBooks Pro and greater versions support fixed percentages, but only QuickBooks Premier and Enterprise support the per item price level. Where is this discount applied if Price Levels are enabled in QuickBooks preferences? The discount is applied to the sales price of the item. If the price level is applied to a customer, it automatically adjusts the Rate and Amount columns for applicable line items in a QuickBooks Sales Order form, Invoice form, etc. for that customer. The QuickBooks user could still select a different price level. However, the customer price level simply establishes a default price. If no price level is applied to the customer, then the QuickBooks user can apply a price level by clicking the dropdown list of price levels that appears next to the Rate column. The default in this case is simply the sales price established for the item. Notice that this value supports both positive and negative values. For example, a value of 20 would increase the price by 20% and value of -10 would decrease the price by 10%.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

adjust_percentage.description:
If you don’t want to apply a custom price (for price levels) or custom rate (for billing rates), you can apply an adjusted price discount using the pair of fields AdjustPercentage and AdjustRelativeTo (AdjustBillingRateRelativeTo for billing rates). You specify the percentage discount or increase in the AdjustPercentage field and the price/rate to be discounted (standard item price, item cost, or the item’s current custom price) in the AdjustRelativeTo fieldTo field. Notice that this value supports both positive and negative values. For example, a value of 20 would increase the price by 20% and value of -10 would decrease the price by 10%.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

adjust_relative_to.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a flat custom price (flat amount or percentage) or you could use PriceLevelAdjustment to apply a price discount based on either the current custom price, the standard price of the item, or the cost of the item. You specify the price discount in the AdjustPercentage field and the price to be discounted (standard item price, item cost, or the item’s current customer price) in the AdjustRelativeTo fieldTo field.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (CustomPrice) or a fixed discount percentage (CustomPricePercent). Alternatively, instead of a flat custom price or discount, you could apply a price discount based on either the current custom price, the standard price of the item, or the cost of the item.

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

custom_price_percent.description:
When you create a price level, you have the option to create it with a custom price that is either a fixed amount (CustomPrice) or a fixed discount percentage (CustomPricePercent).

Choose exactly one of: the set (`custom_price`, `custom_price_percent`), or the set (`adjust_percentage`, `adjust_relative_to`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. parameters.description:
Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: Don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: account_filter

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants.

full_name_with_children.description: Allows you to filter for data that relates to the specified object and its descendants. For names that don’t have children, FullNameWithChildren is exactly the same as FullName.

from_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. Desktop QuickBooks supports 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07; QBOE supports 1900-01-01T00:00:00 through 9999-12-31T00:00:00. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00. In QBFC, use the asDateOnly parameter to control date-only versus date-time behavior.

to_modified_date.description: Filters results to objects modified on or before this timestamp. Desktop QuickBooks supports 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07; QBOE supports 1900-01-01T00:00:00 through 9999-12-31T00:00:00. If only a date is provided, time defaults to end-of-day (23:59:59). Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: ref_number_filter

ref_number.description: RefNumber is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate RefNumber when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

parameters.description:

Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: ref_number_range_filter

from_ref_number.description: The first RefNumber in the search range. If FromRefNumber is omitted, the range will begin with first number on the list.

to_ref_number.description: The final RefNumber in the search range. If ToRefNumber is omitted, the range will end with last number on the list.

parameters.description:
Filters according to the original transaction dates.

Choose at most one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). from_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or after this date. Both FromTxnDate and ToTxnDate must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999.If you omit FromTxnDate, it will be set to 1970-01-01 (1969-12-31 PST).

to_txn_date.description: Selects transactions created on or before this date. Both ToTxnDate and FromTxnDate must be between 01/01/1901 and 12/31/9999. If you omit ToTxnDate, it will be set to 2038-01-19 (2038-01-18 PST).

date_macro.description: DateMacro filters by transaction date (not last-modified date). Do not combine DateMacro with FromModifiedDate/ToModifiedDate in the same query filter set.

parameters.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand. It must be an absolute http or https URL. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address.
parameters.name: webhook_url

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

put.description:
qbXML: `ReceivePaymentModRq`, from qbXML 6.0. The `receive_payment_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Modifies a receive payment transaction. If you save QBMS credit card data in your ReceivePayments, this Mod request allows you to capture a previously authorized credit card charge. The way this works is that the ReceivePaymentAdd would contain the QBMS CreditCardTxnInfo aggregate with the CreditCardTxnType set to “Authorization,” which causes QB to internally mark the transaction as pending. When the capture transaction is performed later, in QBMS, that capture transaction can be saved into QuickBooks via this Mod request, as you are modifying the original ReceivePayment but changing its CreditCardTxnType from”Authorization” to “Capture.” This mod operation results in the removal of the pending status and the posting of this receive payment.

Notice that the reconciliation data fields (ReconBatchID, PaymentGroupingCode, PaymentStatus, TxnAuthorizationTime, TxnAuthorizationStamp, ClientTransID) are optional ONLY if the CreditCardTxnType is “Authorization” because authorizations don’t have such data. If the type is “Charge”, then those reconciliation fields must be supplied or you will get a runtime error.

The following list describes what you can and can’t do with this request.

- Modify RefNumber or Memo.
- Modify (not clear) the CustomerRef field for a payment that wasn’t electronically processed.
- Modify (not clear) the ARAccountRef.
- Modify (not clear) the TxnDate.
- Modify or clear the TotalAmount.
- Modify or clear the PaymentMethodRef.
- Modify, (not clear) the DepositToAccountRef
- Change the payment amount applied to an invoice. For a receive payment transaction that has been applied to several existing invoices, redistribute the payment amounts applied to the invoices.
- Change the discount amount applied to particular invoice.
- You can’t change the credit amount applied to an invoice.
- Apply the payment to a different invoice, including a discount and a credit. Apply the payment amount to a different invoice. Apply a discount, and a credit. The existing distribution is cleared, except for any credit that may have been applied.
- Modify QBMS credit card information
- You can’t auto apply payment.
- Apply an additional credit to an invoice.

The following notes might be of use to you:

Changing the A/R account

If a ReceivePaymentMod specifies the ARAccountRef field without specifying any change to the way the payment amount is applied (no AppliedToTxnMod aggregates are specified), then the request will fail. The A/R account on the receive payment transaction must match the A/R account on the invoices you are paying.

Links

Links between transactions need a particular attention. Received Payments can be linked with receivables, such as invoices. Make sure that after modifying a received payment which is linked to another transaction, the links aren’t damaged. Changing a simple field, such as Memo, preserves existing links. Specifying the AppliedToTxnMod aggregate clears existing links, as described in the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide ([PDF](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/logged-in-content/QBSDK_ProGuide.pdf), 9.6 MB) chapter on modifying transactions.

The impact of permissions settings

Users must have Sales and Accounts Receivable and Changing and deleting transactions permissions set to yes to modify a receive payment transaction. Otherwise, SDK returns an INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS error (status ID = 3260). If the transaction date is before the closing date, they need also the Changing and deleting transactions before closing date permission. Otherwise, SDK will returns CANNOT_MODIFY_BEFORE_CLOSING_DATE error (status ID = 3171).

Impact of preference settings There are 3 preference settings that affect the behavior of the Receive Payment form in the UI. They are: Automatically apply payments, Automatically calculate payments, and Use Undeposited Funds as a default deposit to account. None of these preference settings affects the processing of the ReceivePaymentMod request.

Other Considerations

If you want to change the payment amount, you must specify the new amount. The amount won’t be calculated based on the selected invoices.

Conversely, this request doesn’t auto apply the payment amount to the unpaid invoices. If you want to to edit the existing payment distribution, you must specify the individual invoices to which the payment should be applied.

The “Use Undeposited Funds as Default” option doesn’t affect this request. If you want to edit the existing DepositToAccountRef, you must specify the new account–this field can’t simply be cleared.

Specific error conditions that pertain to this feature

If user tries to clear a field that can’t be cleared, this request returns error 3190: Can’t clear required element.

discount_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where this discount is tracked. In a request, if a DiscountAccountRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

discount_class_ref.description: Class reference used in the Discount object.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

payment_amount.description: Represents the amount assigned to a particular receivable. The sum of all PaymentAmount elements in any given receive payment transaction must not be greater than TotalAmount.

applied_amount.description: Amount of a credit that is applied to a customer’s invoice, or amount of a payment that is applied to a particular bill or vendor credit.

credit_txn_id.description: The ID of the credit memo that you are applying to this invoice or bill.

txn_id.description: TxnID is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. TxnID values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

ar_account_ref.description: ARAccountRef points to an Accounts Receivable account. If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

credit_card_txn_info_mod.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element CreditCardTxnInputInfo” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “CreditCardTxnResultInfo” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info_mod.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info_mod.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq. You should also save this transaction ID and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you are intending to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

customer_ref.description: CustomerRef identifies a customer or customer job. If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. In SalesReceipt and ReceivePayment, it identifies who receives credit. In TimeTracking, it identifies who the time can be billed to and is required in TimeTrackingAdd when IsBillable is true. In ExpenseLineAdd, if AccountRef is A/P, CustomerRef must be a vendor; otherwise it must be a customer.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

deposit_to_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where these funds will be (or have been) deposited. In a ReceivePaymentAdd request, the default is Undeposited Funds if this isn’t included in the request. In a request, if a DepositToAccountRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

exchange_rate.description: ExchangeRate is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. You can supply a rate when adding transactions, but QuickBooks does not provide rates through the SDK. If your home currency is USD and internet access is available, rates can be downloaded in the QuickBooks UI via Lists > Currency > Activities > Download Latest Exchange Rates.

memo.description: The beginning of this memo will appear in reports that show details of this receive payment.

payment_method_ref.description: PaymentMethodRef identifies how a payment is made (for example, cash, check, or card type). If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

ref_number.description: RefNumber is a user-managed transaction reference (for example, a check number). It can be edited and is not guaranteed to be globally unique. Some transaction types auto-populate RefNumber when omitted, based on QuickBooks preferences and numbering state.

request_id.description: Your own label for the request, sent to QuickBooks as its qbXML `requestID` and echoed in the raw answer (`response_xml`); optional, since the answer's webhook already carries the request's `id`.

total_amount.description: Total amount of money received. For ReceivePaymentAdd, the sum of the PaymentAmount amounts (in the AppliedToTxnAdd aggregates that are included) can’t be greater than the TotalAmount, or you will receive an error.

txn_date.description: The date of the transaction. In some cases, if you leave TxnDate out of an -Add message, QuickBooks will prefill TxnDate with the date of the last-saved transaction of the same type.

txn_id.description: TxnID is the unique QuickBooks identifier for a transaction. Use it to reference that transaction in later requests. TxnID values are transaction-specific and should not be reused across unrelated transaction types.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

post.description:
qbXML: `SalesOrderAddRq`, from qbXML 2.1. The `sales_order_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds a sales order. A sales order tracks inventory that is on back order for a customer. In QuickBooks, sales orders and invoices use similar fields, and a sales order can be “converted” into an invoice (by linking the invoice to the sales order) once the inventory is in stock.

You can create Sales Orders only with QuickBooks Premier and above. However, if you are accessing a company file created in Premier and above from a lesser edition of QuickBooks (such as Pro), you should be able to do queries against SalesOrders and also Mods.

Since a sales order is a non-posting transaction, QuickBooks business logic doesn’t require the sales tax information at the point where the SalesOrder is added. (In the OSR this is an optional field.) However, the sales tax item IS required for the invoice. So if the SalesOrder doesn’t have a sales tax item set for it, you need to modify it so that it does have one before you create an invoice using that sales order.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs the answer to it once QuickBooks has answered (see the `answered` callback: its own payload, not this document). `links.self` returns this document on demand, with `response_json` filled in.

post.description:
Verify `X-QUBE-Signature`, answer 2xx within 5 seconds, then branch on `state`:

* `response_received` -- QuickBooks accepted it: `response_json` is `status: "success"` with `data`, or, when there is nothing to show, QuickBooks' `message` (a query that matched nothing is a success, not an error). When QuickBooks carried it out but warned about something, `response_json.warning` has its `code` and `message`: `530`, for one, means a field you sent is not supported by the customer's QuickBooks and was not saved.
* `error` -- it failed for good. With `error.error_type` `quickbooks_business_error`, QuickBooks refused the request: `response_json` is `status: "error"`, and `response_json.error.code` is the status code to branch on. Otherwise QuickBooks never answered it: `xml_error` (the request itself was rejected, and will be again as sent) or `unexpected_error` (the Web Connector's log says more). A connection problem never ends here; it is `retryable`, below.
* `retryable` -- the Web Connector could not get it into QuickBooks (QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not this connection's, or a window in QuickBooks was in the way), so nothing was applied. QuBe Sync keeps trying on the Web Connector's runs, so don't resend: show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. This webhook comes when the error first appears or changes, not on every try. If you no longer want the request, discard it (`POST /connections/{connection_id}/queued_requests/{id}/discard`).
* `timed_out` -- abandoned without an answer. QuickBooks may still have applied it, so look before sending an add again.
* `discarded` -- your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up. QuickBooks never got it, so nothing was applied.

An iterated query sends one webhook per page, all with the same `id`; `iteration_state` is `done` on the last one. Deliveries can arrive out of order and, after a retry, more than once: key on `page_request_id` and treat a repeat as already handled.

If webhooks stop arriving altogether, the Web Connector on the customer's PC has most likely stopped calling in; requests wait until it does. Intuit's guide to its errors: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

schema.description: POSTed to `webhook_url` as JSON, signed with `X-QUBE-Signature` (`t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your app's webhook secret>`).

error.description: Set when `state` is `error` or `retryable` (and kept if a `retryable` request is then discarded). `error_type` says where it failed; `user_message` is safe to show an end user; `error_code` is QuickBooks' own status code for a business error, `hresult` the Web Connector's for a connection/XML error; `debug_message` is for you.

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known.

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error.

error_type.description: `quickbooks_business_error`: QuickBooks refused the request -- `response_json.error` has its code. `quickbooks_connection_error`: the Web Connector ran on the customer's PC but could not get the request into QuickBooks, so nothing was applied -- QuickBooks was not running, the company file was not open or not the one this connection belongs to, or a window or message box open in QuickBooks was in the way. Only the customer can fix that, and `user_message` tells them how. `xml_error`: QuickBooks could not parse the qbXML; sent again as-is, it fails again. `unexpected_error`: anything else. Web Connector problems on the customer's PC (its password, log file, the .QWC file) never reach QuBe Sync as an error: the Web Connector just stops calling in, and requests wait. Intuit's guide for those: https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/open-programs/fix-common-web-connector-errors-quickbooks-desktop/L9slolvg0_US_en_US

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT (e.g. `0x80040400`), for a connection or XML error. Informational: branch on `error_type`, not on this.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector.

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user.

id.description: The request's id, as the 201 returned it. For an iterated query, every page carries the first page's id here.

iteration_state.description: `continue`: more pages will follow, each its own webhook. `done`: this was the last page. `max_sandbox_iterations_reached`: a sandbox app's page limit stopped the iteration.

page_request_id.description: This page's own id. Equal to `id` except on later pages of an iterated query.

response_xml.description: QuickBooks' raw qbXML answer. `response_json` is the same, summarized.

sandbox.description: Whether the app is a sandbox app.

state.description: `response_received`: QuickBooks accepted it; read `response_json`. `error`: it failed for good -- see `error`, and `response_json.error` for a QuickBooks business error. `retryable`: QuickBooks could not be reached and QuBe Sync keeps trying; show the customer `error.user_message` so they can fix it. `timed_out`: the request was abandoned and will not be answered. `discarded`: your app discarded it before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; the same `t` the signature covers.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else is retried, up to 5 attempts.
